issues.title: Feature: Phase 7 — Template SPA semantic search integration (backlog)
issues.body:
**Parent epic:** E-search-tmpl — Semantic search companion module

## What
Integrate the kbexplorer-search service with the kbexplorer-template SPA, enabling
semantic search from the Ctrl-K palette and HUD search buttons.

## Why
Makes semantic search feel native in the visual explorer — the existing text search
in the palette would be augmented with semantic results from the search service.

## Scope
- Connect the search palette (Ctrl-K) to the search service API when configured.
- Display semantic results alongside existing text matches.
- Navigate to the matched node on selection.
- Config flag in config.yaml: `features.semanticSearch: true` + service URL.
- Graceful degradation: if the service is unavailable, text search works as before.

## Acceptance
- Ctrl-K palette shows semantic results when a search service is configured.
- Selecting a semantic result navigates to the correct node.
- Without a service, the palette works identically to today.

**Blocked by:** F5 (needs the search service running).

issues.title: Feature: Phase 6 — Graph-aware ranking and related-node suggestions (backlog)
issues.body:
**Parent epic:** E-search-tmpl — Semantic search companion module

## What
Enhance search results with graph-aware ranking signals and related-node suggestions.
A search hit for a node should also surface its neighbors, parent, and cluster siblings
as contextual suggestions.

## Why
Graph-aware search is the differentiator: results know their place in the knowledge
graph, not just their text similarity. This enables "explore around this result" UX.

## Scope
- Boost results whose neighbors also match the query (graph proximity signal).
- Include related nodes in SearchResult (top-3 neighbors by edge weight).
- Cluster-coherence bonus: results in the same cluster as other hits rank higher.
- Hierarchy-aware snippets: include parent node title in snippet context.

## Acceptance
- A query that matches a node AND its parent ranks higher than an isolated match.
- Related-node suggestions are relevant and come from the graph, not just text similarity.

**Blocked by:** F4 (needs the base query engine).

issues.title: Feature: Phase 5 — Localhost search service (HTTP API)
issues.body:
**Parent epic:** E-search-tmpl — Semantic search companion module

## What
A lightweight HTTP server that serves semantic search results from checked-in artifacts.
Runs locally during development or as a deployable service in production.

## Why
Enables real-time semantic search during development (alongside `kbexplorer dev`) and
provides a deployable API endpoint for hosted search.

## Scope
- HTTP server (Node.js, no framework dependency — use `node:http` or minimal fastify).
- `POST /search` endpoint: `{ query, limit?, cluster?, entityType?, minScore? } → SearchResult[]`.
- `GET /health` endpoint: service status + index metadata.
- Loads artifacts at startup; auto-reloads on file change (dev mode).
- CORS headers for localhost development.

## Acceptance
- `curl -X POST localhost:3457/search -d '{"query":"audit"}'` returns ranked results.
- Health endpoint reports model name, unit count, and dimensions.

**Blocked by:** F4 (needs the query engine).

issues.title: Task: Add optional FAISS index for fast k-NN search
issues.body:
**Parent feature:** F4 — Vector index loading + semantic query engine

## Scope
Create `src/faiss-engine.ts` (optional, peer dependency):
- Use `faiss-node` as an optional peer dependency.
- Build a FAISS IndexFlatIP (inner product for normalized vectors) from artifact vectors.
- `FaissSearchEngine` implements the same `SearchEngine` interface.
- Auto-detect: if faiss-node is available, use it; otherwise fall back to pure-JS.
- The FAISS index is built at startup from the portable artifact vectors — it is NOT
  the source of truth, just a runtime acceleration.

## Validation criteria
FAISS engine returns identical results to pure-JS engine (same ranking order).

## Evidence-based completion criteria
- [ ] Test: FAISS and pure-JS engines return the same top-5 results for a given query
- [ ] Test: when faiss-node is not installed, the fallback engine is used without error
- [ ] Test: FAISS index build completes in < 1s for 1000 vectors

issues.title: Task: Implement pure-JS cosine similarity search engine
issues.body:
**Parent feature:** F4 — Vector index loading + semantic query engine

## Scope
Create `src/search-engine.ts`:
- `createSearchEngine(artifacts: EmbeddingArtifact, provider: EmbeddingProvider): SearchEngine`
- `SearchEngine.search(query: string, opts?: { limit?, cluster?, entityType?, minScore? }): Promise<SearchResult[]>`
- Embed the query via the same provider used for indexing.
- Compute cosine similarity against all vectors (brute force for pure JS).
- Return top-k results mapped to SearchResult objects with full metadata from units.
- Apply optional filters (cluster, entityType, minScore threshold).
- Sort by score descending.

## Validation criteria
Search returns correctly-ranked results with full metadata.

## Evidence-based completion criteria
- [ ] Test: search("audit validation") returns nodes with "audit" in title/content ranked first
- [ ] Test: cluster filter restricts results to the specified cluster
- [ ] Test: minScore threshold excludes low-relevance results
- [ ] Test: SearchResult contains nodeId, title, cluster, score, snippet, connections

issues.title: Feature: Phase 4 — Vector index loading + semantic query engine
issues.body:
**Parent epic:** E-search-tmpl — Semantic search companion module

## What
Implement the query engine that loads checked-in artifacts, builds an in-memory vector
index, embeds incoming queries, and returns ranked `SearchResult` objects.

## Why
This is the index consumption role. The engine must be fast (sub-100ms for typical
knowledge bases) and return kbexplorer-native results with full graph metadata.

## Scope
- Load artifacts from disk (units.json + vectors.json).
- Build an in-memory vector index (FAISS via faiss-node, or a pure-JS fallback for
  portability).
- Query: embed the query text → k-nearest-neighbor search → map to SearchResults.
- Filters: by cluster, by entity type, by score threshold.
- Pure-JS cosine similarity fallback for environments without native FAISS.

## Acceptance
- Query returns top-k results ranked by relevance.
- Cluster/type filters work correctly.
- Fallback mode works without FAISS native binary.

**Blocked by:** F3 (needs serialized artifacts to load).

issues.title: Task: Implement drift detection gate (--check mode)
issues.body:
**Parent feature:** F3 — Artifact serialization, checked-in format, and drift gate

## Scope
Create `src/drift.ts`:
- `checkDrift(artifactDir: string, graph: KBGraph, config: SearchConfig): DriftResult`
- Re-extracts SearchUnits from the current graph (no embedding API call).
- Compares extracted units against committed `units.json` (by canonical stringify).
- Compares content hash against `index-meta.json.contentHash`.
- Returns `{ fresh: boolean, staleUnits: string[], missingUnits: string[], extraUnits: string[] }`.
- Exits non-zero when units diverge OR content hash mismatches.
- Never calls the embedding provider — purely deterministic.

## Validation criteria
Drift detection is purely offline and catches stale artifacts.

## Evidence-based completion criteria
- [ ] Test: check with fresh artifacts returns { fresh: true }
- [ ] Test: check after adding a node returns { fresh: false, missingUnits: [...] }
- [ ] Test: check after modifying node content returns { fresh: false, staleUnits: [...] }
- [ ] Test: no network calls are made during check

issues.title: Task: Implement artifact writer with deterministic serialization
issues.body:
**Parent feature:** F3 — Artifact serialization, checked-in format, and drift gate

## Scope
Create `src/artifacts.ts`:
- `writeArtifacts(dir: string, units: SearchUnit[], vectors: EmbeddingVector[], config: SearchConfig): void`
- Writes three files to `dir/`:
  - `index-meta.json`: `{ version: 1, model, dimensions, unitCount, contentHash, generatedFrom }`
  - `units.json`: SearchUnit[] with sorted keys, sorted by unitId.
  - `vectors.json`: EmbeddingVector[] sorted by unitId, vectors as number arrays.
- All JSON uses `canonicalStringify`: sorted keys, 2-space indent, trailing newline.
- `readArtifacts(dir: string)`: deserialize back.
- `computeContentHash(graph: KBGraph): string`: SHA-256 of the canonical graph.

## Validation criteria
Write + read round-trip is byte-identical; hash is deterministic.

## Evidence-based completion criteria
- [ ] Test: writeArtifacts then readArtifacts returns identical data
- [ ] Test: two writes of same data produce byte-identical files (diff returns empty)
- [ ] Test: computeContentHash on same graph returns same hash
- [ ] Test: index-meta.json contains correct unit count and model name

issues.title: Feature: Phase 3 — Artifact serialization, checked-in format, and drift gate
issues.body:
**Parent epic:** E-search-tmpl — Semantic search companion module

## What
Define the on-disk artifact format for checked-in search state, implement deterministic
serialization, and provide a CI-grade drift detection gate.

## Why
The repository owns the semantic search corpus. Artifacts must be deterministic (identical
input → byte-identical output), reviewable in PRs, and verifiable in CI. This is the
same principle behind `kbexplorer derive --check` — the search equivalent.

## Scope
- Artifact file format: `search-artifacts/` directory containing:
  - `index-meta.json`: version, model, dimensions, unit count, content hash.
  - `units.json`: SearchUnit array (no vectors — readable, reviewable).
  - `vectors.json`: EmbeddingVector array (or a binary format for large indexes).
- Deterministic serialization: sorted keys, stable array order, no timestamps.
- Drift detection: `--check` flag that compares committed artifacts against a fresh
  extraction (without calling the embedding API) and exits non-zero on mismatch.
- Content-hash computation for the source graph (so artifacts know what they were built from).

## Acceptance
- Write + read round-trip produces byte-identical artifacts.
- `--check` detects when content changed but artifacts are stale.
- `--check` passes when artifacts are fresh.

**Blocked by:** F2 (needs embedding generation to produce the artifacts).

issues.title: Task: Implement batch embedding generator with content-hash caching
issues.body:
**Parent feature:** F2 — Pluggable embedding provider + batch generation

## Scope
Create `src/embed.ts`:
- `generateEmbeddings(units: SearchUnit[], provider: EmbeddingProvider, opts?): Promise<EmbeddingVector[]>`
- Process units in batches (configurable batchSize, default 100).
- Compute SHA-256 hash of each SearchUnit.text; if a previous artifact has the same
  hash + model + dimensions, reuse the existing vector (skip the API call).
- Rate limiting: configurable delay between batches (default 100ms).
- Progress callback for CLI integration.

## Validation criteria
Batch generation works with mocked provider; caching skips unchanged units.

## Evidence-based completion criteria
- [ ] Test: 150 units with batchSize=100 makes exactly 2 provider.embed() calls
- [ ] Test: re-running with identical units and a cached artifact makes 0 embed() calls
- [ ] Test: changing one unit text re-embeds only that unit
- [ ] Test: progress callback fires with correct counts

issues.title: Feature: Phase 2 — Pluggable embedding provider + batch generation
issues.body:
**Parent epic:** E-search-tmpl — Semantic search companion module

## What
Implement the embedding provider abstraction and a default OpenAI provider, plus
batch embedding generation that converts SearchUnits into EmbeddingVectors.

## Why
Embedding generation must be pluggable — different teams use different models (OpenAI,
Cohere, local Ollama, etc.). The abstraction lets the artifact format stay stable while
the model varies.

## Scope
- `EmbeddingProvider` interface with `embed(texts: string[]): Promise<number[][]>`.
- OpenAI provider implementation (text-embedding-3-small default).
- Batch generation: process SearchUnits in configurable batch sizes with rate limiting.
- Content-hash keyed caching: skip re-embedding unchanged SearchUnits.
- Provider registry: resolve by name from config.

## Acceptance
- OpenAI provider generates embeddings for a batch of texts.
- Re-running on unchanged SearchUnits skips embedding (uses cached vectors).
- A custom provider can be registered and used instead of OpenAI.

**Blocked by:** F1 (needs SearchUnit extraction).

issues.title: Task: Implement KBGraph → SearchUnit[] extraction with markdown parsing
issues.body:
**Parent feature:** F1 — KBGraph → SearchUnit extraction pipeline

## Scope
Create `src/extract.ts` with:
- `extractSearchUnits(graph: KBGraph, config?: ChunkingConfig): SearchUnit[]`
- Strip HTML from `node.content`, use `node.rawContent` (markdown) as primary text.

- Skip nodes with empty rawContent (structural/tree nodes).

Unit tests pass with a fixture KBGraph; output is deterministic and correctly shaped.

## Evidence-based completion criteria
- [ ] Test: extractSearchUnits on a 5-node fixture returns 5+ SearchUnits with correct nodeIds

issues.title: Feature: Phase 1 — KBGraph → SearchUnit extraction pipeline
issues.body:
**Parent epic:** E-search-tmpl — Semantic search companion module

## What
Implement the extraction pipeline that converts a `KBGraph` (nodes, edges, clusters)
into an array of `SearchUnit` objects — the atomic searchable entities.

## Why
The search module must understand the kbexplorer content model deeply, not just treat
nodes as raw text. SearchUnits carry graph-aware metadata (cluster, hierarchy, connections,
entity type, identity URN) so that search results can be placed back into the graph.

## Scope
- Parse KBNode content (rawContent markdown) into searchable text.
- Chunk long nodes into multiple SearchUnits with configurable max-token limits and overlap.
- Enrich each SearchUnit with graph context: cluster, parent, connections list, entity type.
- Handle all NodeSource types (authored, structured, derived, issue, file, etc.).
- Deterministic output: same graph → same SearchUnits (stable ordering, no randomness).
- Unit tests with fixture graphs.

## Acceptance
- A KBGraph with 20+ nodes produces correctly-shaped SearchUnits.
- Long nodes are chunked; short nodes produce a single SearchUnit.
- Graph metadata (cluster, connections, parent) is correctly propagated.
- Output is deterministic (two runs on the same input → identical output).

**Blocked by:** F0 (needs the core types and package skeleton).

issues.title: Epic: Semantic search companion module (kbexplorer-search)
issues.body:
## What
kbexplorer defines a structured knowledge graph: authored markdown nodes, frontmatter
metadata, clusters, hierarchy, relationships, and source-aware content. This Epic creates
a companion `@anokye-labs/kbexplorer-search` module that understands that model and turns
it into a semantic search corpus — without making the visual graph app or the core CLI
responsible for vector-search infrastructure.

The module has two complementary roles:

1. **Index production** — reads the kbexplorer content model, derives searchable units from
   the graph (SearchUnits), generates embeddings via a pluggable provider, and writes
   checked-in search artifacts (embeddings, index metadata, node-to-vector mappings).
   These artifacts become part of the repository — they travel with branches, PRs, reviews,
   releases, and deployments.

2. **Index consumption** — loads the checked-in artifacts, builds an efficient vector index
   (FAISS or similar), embeds incoming queries using the same configured model, and returns
   kbexplorer-native results: node IDs, titles, paths, clusters, snippets, scores, and
   graph-aware context.

The repository owns the semantic search corpus; the service only provides query execution.
Embeddings and mapping files are durable, reviewable build outputs tied to the exact
version of the kbexplorer graph.

## Why
Search results should be graph-aware — they know node identity, cluster membership,
hierarchy, authored connections, source citations, and page structure. A query for
"how does audit validation work?" should return the relevant kbexplorer node, its
relationship to nearby concepts, and enough metadata to place the result back into the
graph. This makes semantic search feel native to kbexplorer rather than bolted on.

The design also fits the development workflow: a contributor changes content, runs the
search index builder, commits both content and updated search artifacts. CI verifies
artifact freshness. A hosted service deploys directly from repository state.

## Adopted model / approach
- Separate `@anokye-labs/kbexplorer-search` npm package in a new repo.
- Consumes `KBNode`/`KBGraph`/`KBConfig` types from kbexplorer-core (or inlined
  initially until kbexplorer-core is published).
- Pluggable embedding providers (OpenAI, local models, configurable).
- Checked-in artifacts are deterministic (sorted keys, no timestamps, content-hash keyed).
- FAISS (via faiss-node or similar) as the default runtime index, but the design does not
  depend solely on a native binary index as the only source of truth.
- Phased delivery: extraction → embedding → artifacts → query engine → CLI → service.

## Scope boundaries
- In: the search module repo, its core types, extraction pipeline, embedding provider
  abstraction, artifact format, query engine, CLI commands, and localhost service mode.
- Out: kbexplorer-template UI integration for search results (future work),
  kbexplorer-core dependency (tracked by sibling Epic in template),
  production hosted service infrastructure (backlog).

## Success definition
A contributor can: (1) point kbexplorer-search at a kbexplorer content directory,
(2) generate deterministic search artifacts, (3) commit them alongside content,
(4) query semantically and receive graph-aware results with node IDs, clusters, and
scores, (5) run a CI drift gate that verifies artifacts match the current graph.

## Children
Features F0–F7 below. Relates to `anokye-labs/kbexplorer-cli` sibling Epic
(CLI command integration).

issues.title: Epic: Decouple kbexplorer subsystems & enable pluggable providers/representations
issues.body:
## What
Today the three subsystems — system-of-record + providers, the resource-graph-engine,
and the representation/rendering subsystem — are entangled: two fat loaders duplicate
~150 lines of post-processing, there is no first-class system-of-record abstraction,
3rd-party providers cannot actually load (hardcoded plugin switch), representation
styling is baked into core data types, and the SPA is the only output format. Target: a
clean 4-layer pipeline — **Sources → Providers → Engine (pure `KBGraph`) → Representation
registry** — backed by a shared `@anokye-labs/kbexplorer-core` contracts package, so
authors can bring their own local or 3rd-party providers, sources, and representations
without forking core.

## Why
Extensibility is the headline goal: "people should be able to use this and pull in their
own local or 3rd party providers." Decoupling the subsystems is the prerequisite.

## Adopted model / approach
- Shared contracts live in a **separate repo/package** `@anokye-labs/kbexplorer-core`.
- **Affordances are per-*retrieval* and situational** (see §4A of the plan): a source
  declares a possible universe; each retrieved resource carries the affordances allowed
  *now* + hypermedia links. Staging area is a first-class linked resource. **Git ≠ GitHub.**
- Provider loading is **local-ES-module-first**, then 3rd-party npm.
- `llm-context` representation is **neighbor-anchored & navigable** — never the whole graph.
- Each phase keeps graph output **byte-identical** until a seam is intentionally flipped.

## Scope boundaries
- In: phases 0–6 in the template (engine/providers/representation are here).
- Out: CLI-side adoption (Epic in `anokye-labs/kbexplorer-cli`); optional graph store (F7, backlog);
  the net-new docs+showcase repo content beyond standing it up (Feature: docs).

## Success definition
A third party can register a local ES-module provider and a custom representation via
config, render `--as json-ld|llm-context`, and the self-repo graph is byte-identical to
the Phase-0 golden snapshot at every step until a seam is deliberately flipped.

## Children
Features F0, F1, F2, F3, F4, F5a, F5b, F6, F7, F-docs below.
Relates to `anokye-labs/kbexplorer-cli` sibling Epic (CLI adoption).

**Gap E.** The template is pre-1.0 with no reproducible pinning story. `package.json` `version` is still `0.0.0`, and only a single repo tag (`v0.1.0`) exists; `doctor` warns "Template tracks branch `main` — consider pinning to a release tag," but there's no tag to pin to.

### Scope
- Bump the template `package.json` `version` to a real release version.
- Cut a tagged release of the template (immutable tag) and write release notes.
- Publish a CLI↔template compatibility matrix (which template tag works with which CLI version).
- Align `doctor` guidance so a vendor-pinned install referencing an immutable tag no longer triggers the branch-tracking warning.

### Acceptance
- A vendor-pinned install references an immutable release tag.
- `doctor` no longer warns about branch tracking when pinned to a tag.

_Cross-repo note: the CLI side (`init --ref vX.Y.Z` tag resolution) lives in `anokye-labs/kbexplorer-cli`. Part of the kbexplorer-template adoption-readiness epic (#273)._

issues.title: Feature H: First-class service + decision kinds (viewers + edge rules)
issues.body:
**Gap H.** A services monorepo's core entities include **services** (repo service → owning team, ServiceTree id, catalog-info path, repo path) and **decisions** (ADRs). Neither has a bespoke kind/viewer today — both fall back to `GenericStructuredView`. The spine kinds in `src/engine/content-model/register.ts` cover person/squad/workstream/mission/priority/cycle/org/team/system-of-record only.

**Decision: build first-class kinds** (not the doc-only fallback path).

### Scope
- Register `service` + `decision` as spine kinds in `register.ts` (open node-type + viewer registries — no core union edits).
- Add `ServiceView` + `DecisionView` in `src/views/viewers/` (className-styled, SSR-safe), bound via `registerContentModelTypes()`.
- Add edge rules in `content-model/schema/edges.yaml`:
  - `service` `owned-by` → team; `service` `tracked-in` → system-of-record.
  - `decision` `decided-by` → person; `decision` `affects` → workstream/mission.
- Add example entity files under `content-model/services/` and `content-model/decisions/`, plus conventions/lifecycle entries.
- Viewer-registry + spine-viewer unit tests.

### Acceptance
- A `service` node renders ownership + a ServiceTree/catalog link.
- A `decision` node renders deciders + context.
- Achieved without core edits (per the open node-type registry); all FK edges resolve and pass `validate`/`derive --check`.

_Implementation targets `main`. Part of the kbexplorer-template adoption-readiness epic (#273)._

issues.title: Feature C: Navigable people / org-chart (PersonView links + reports-to tree layout)
issues.body:
**Gap C (top template priority for our adoption).** kbexplorer has a `person` kind, `reports-to`/`leads` edges and a `PersonView`, but the people/org-chart experience is bring-your-own: `PersonView` renders `manager`/`reports-to` as **plain text**, and there is **no reports-to tree layout** for navigating a hundreds-person org.

The `person-manager → reports-to` foreign-key edge already exists in `content-model/schema/edges.yaml`, so this is primarily **view-layer** work plus a documented contract for feeding person descriptors from an external (MS Graph) pipeline.

### Sub-tasks
- **C1** — make `PersonView` `manager` / `team` / `reports-to` **navigable graph links** (reuse the existing `NodeLink` pattern; resolve target to the person node id/URN).
- **C2** — add a **reports-to tree layout** that scales to a hundreds-person org.
- **C3** — document the supported **BYO person-descriptor / derived-JSON-LD** feed contract so an external pipeline can supply `person` nodes that pass validation.

### Acceptance
- A hundreds-person org renders as a navigable reports-to tree.
- `PersonView` reporting line is clickable and opens the manager's node.
- Reorg/provenance feeding is documented against a stable, validated contract.

_Implementation targets `main`. Part of the kbexplorer-template adoption-readiness epic (#273)._

issues.title: Epic: kbexplorer-template adoption-readiness for gaming-microsoft/personalization
issues.body:
Tracking epic for the **template-side** changes needed to adopt kbexplorer as the org-knowledge foundation in the EMU services monorepo `gaming-microsoft/personalization`.

Source: the consolidated adoption-gaps draft (gaps A–H). This epic covers only the **[template]**-tagged gaps — **B, C, E, F, H**. CLI-only gaps (A `validate`, D `init --yes`, G EMU CI recipe) live in `anokye-labs/kbexplorer-cli` and are referenced only as cross-repo blockers.

### Reconciliation against current `main` (the gaps doc is partly stale)
- **B — content-model schema files & vocabulary**: now **largely shipped** on `main` (`content-model/` tree at repo root: `teamops.yaml`, `schema/{conventions,edges,lifecycle}.yaml`, `index/context.jsonld`, `index/vocabulary.jsonld`, entity files; plus `docs/work-graph-vocabulary.md`). Remaining template work is verify-and-close; the `init --content-model` scaffolder is CLI-side.
- **C — navigable people / org-chart**: **OPEN**. `PersonView` renders `manager`/`reports-to` as plain text; no reports-to tree layout. The `person-manager → reports-to` FK edge already exists in `schema/edges.yaml`, so this is view-layer work.
- **E — release tags / version**: **OPEN/partial**. Template `package.json` is still `0.0.0`; only a single repo tag `v0.1.0` exists.
- **F — host-root in vendored installs**: tracked by **#220**. `detectHostRoot()` exists but fails for vendored layouts; land an env/config-driven mechanism.
- **H — `service` + `decision` kinds**: **OPEN**. Not registered (`register.ts` has person/squad/workstream/mission/priority/cycle/org/team/system-of-record only); no `service`/`decision` viewers or edge rules. Decision: build first-class kinds.

### Children
- Feature C — navigable people/org-chart (sub-tasks C1 PersonView links, C2 reports-to tree layout, C3 BYO person-feed contract docs)
- Feature H — first-class `service` + `decision` kinds (viewers + edge rules)
- Feature F — config/env-driven host-root (**#220**)
- Task E — version bump + tagged release + CLI↔template compatibility matrix
- Task B — verify content-model schema-config satisfies the template side; close residual

_Implementation targets `main`. Filed to coordinate ahead of adoption in `gaming-microsoft/personalization`._

issues.title: Remove unused gray-matter dependency (js-yaml Moderate advisory)
issues.body:
`gray-matter` (a direct dependency) bundles `js-yaml@3.14.2`, which is flagged by [GHSA-h67p-54hq-rp68](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-h67p-54hq-rp68) — a Moderate quadratic-complexity DoS. There is no patched 3.x release (everything <= 4.1.1 is vulnerable).

`gray-matter` is not imported anywhere in the codebase, and `yaml`@^2 is already a dependency for any future frontmatter parsing. Removing `gray-matter` eliminates the transitive `js-yaml` 3.x and clears the advisory.

issues.title: Wire the full-loop scenario (layer 4) into a nightly CI job
issues.body:
**Gap surfaced while writing `TESTING.md` (#258).**

Layer 4 of the test pyramid — the full-loop scenario (`e2e/full-loop/actor-regen-render.spec.ts`, run via `npm run test:e2e:full-loop` / `playwright.full-loop.config.ts`) — currently runs **only manually/locally**. No scheduled workflow invokes it:

- `dtu-gitea.yml` (nightly 04:30 UTC) runs only `npm run test:e2e:gitea` (layer 3).
- `visual-regression.yml` and `explore-dtu.yml` cover layers 5 and 6.

So the full-loop never executes in CI, and regressions in the actor→twin→CLI-regen→app-render→verify path would not be caught nightly.

### Options
1. Extend `dtu-gitea.yml` to also run `npm run test:e2e:full-loop` after the gitea suite (shares the Podman bringup; cheapest).
2. Add a dedicated nightly workflow for the full-loop.

Option 1 is likely simplest since the substrate/bringup overlaps. Note the full-loop's default substrate is `static` (`FULL_LOOP_SUBSTRATE=static`); the live-Gitea substrate is still deferred, so wiring it nightly may also be a good moment to wire the gitea substrate.

`TESTING.md` documents this as "tracked separately" and points here.

Part of the testing system established in epic #254.

issues.title: Remote/runtime mode does not ingest the content-model (work-graph nodes absent without a CLI manifest)
issues.body:
Surfaced by the work-graph DTU scenarios (#256 / PR #264).

`loadRemoteKnowledgeBase()` (src/engine/remote-loader.ts) registers `new ContentModelProvider(null)` — a no-op — so in **remote/runtime mode** the content-model (work-graph vocabulary: team/workstream/priority/person/system-of-record from #232) is **not fetched or rendered**. Those nodes only appear in **local-manifest mode** (the CLI writes them into the manifest).

Impact: a runtime-mode deployment (app fetching live from GitHub in-browser, no CLI-built manifest) shows issues/PRs/releases but NOT the organizational layer. Two `.fixme` specs in e2e/gitea/workgraph-mutations.spec.ts document this and can be un-fixme'd when the remote fetch path lands.

Fix: implement a remote content-model fetch (read content-model/ files from the repo via the GitHub API / adapter) and pass a populated `ContentModelProvider` in the remote loader, mirroring the local loader. Relates to the work-graph epic #232.

issues.title: Exploratory-agent harness: scheduled agent sessions probe the DTU and open spec PRs
issues.body: Part of the comprehensive testing epic. Formalize the README's exploratory-agent playbook into a runnable/scheduled harness: bring the DTU up, launch agent session(s) with the probing prompt, have them mutate via actors, find gaps, and open human-reviewed e2e/gitea spec PRs (never auto-committed; assertions in specs, never twins). A workflow_dispatch + nightly entry point that the orchestrator can fire.

issues.title: TESTING.md: the test pyramid + CI orchestration + holdout discipline
issues.body: Part of the comprehensive testing epic. A single TESTING.md (superseding/linking DTU.md) defining the whole pyramid: unit (vitest/node:test) -> static-twin fast e2e (PR gate) -> live-DTU scenarios (nightly) -> full-loop (nightly) -> visual regression -> exploratory-agent. For each layer: what it covers, what twin it uses, where it runs (PR vs nightly vs manual), and the holdout rule. Reconcile the two repos' CI so the split is explicit and consistent.

issues.title: Visual-regression gate: capture-review baseline diff per theme × surface
issues.body: Part of the comprehensive testing epic. Turn the capture-review harness (scripts/capture-review.mjs + BEAUTY.md) into a regression gate: maintain committed baseline screenshots (or hashes/SSIM) per surface x theme, diff new captures against them, fail on meaningful drift, and surface a visual report artifact. Optionally drive captures from twin states so visual + data are tested together. Defines what's a PR gate vs nightly.

issues.title: Work-graph DTU scenarios: team/workstream/release mutations reflected on refresh
issues.body: Part of the comprehensive testing epic. Extend the live-twin scenario suite (e2e/gitea/) beyond issues/PRs to the org layer shipped in #232: an actor edits content-model/teams/*.yaml or workstreams/*.yaml (via the edit-source actor) or cuts a release, and the app reflects the new/changed team, workstream, release, or person node on refresh. New actors as needed (e.g. cut-release). Assertions in specs only.

issues.title: Full-loop deployment scenario: actor → twin → CLI regen → app render → verify
issues.body: Part of the comprehensive testing epic. The single scenario that exercises the real deployment shape end-to-end: a DTU actor mutates the Gitea twin (open issue / cut release / edit team.yaml), the CLI regenerates the manifest **from the twin** (depends on the CLI↔DTU seam, cli repo), the app builds+renders that manifest, and a verify step asserts the mutation is reflected. Lives in e2e/gitea/ (or a new e2e/full-loop/) under the holdout rule. Depends on the CLI↔DTU seam.

issues.title: Epic: Comprehensive testing system — DTU spine across CLI, app, and visual surfaces
issues.body:
## Why

The DTU foundation is live on main: a static GitHub fixture twin (`twins/github/`, the fast PR gate) and a stateful Gitea live twin (`twins/gitea/`, Podman + GitHub→Gitea proxy on `VITE_GH_API_BASE`, scripted actors, nightly). `DTU.md` states the ambition: **local behavioral clones of every external service**, with the **holdout rule** (specs are the holdout set; never code to them).

Today that spine only validates the **app** (browser, remote mode). The **CLI** pipeline (`init/generate/derive/manifest/build`) shells out to `gh` directly and is tested only by unit injection + the static mock — never against the live, mutating twin. There is no **full-loop** test (twin mutates → CLI regenerates → app renders → verify), and the project's other external dependencies — **agent runtimes** (copilot/claude) and **MCP servers** (ADO, SharePoint) — have no twins at all, despite being the backbone of the local-first regeneration the work-repo deployment depends on.

## Outcome

A test pyramid where every external service has a twin and every surface (CLI, app, visual) is exercised against it — the same way a real deployment runs — with a clear PR-gate vs nightly vs exploratory split, all under the holdout discipline.

## The matrix (service × surface)

| Service \ Surface | Unit | App e2e | CLI pipeline | Full loop |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GitHub | ✅ | ✅ static + ✅ live Gitea | 🔴 (no twin path) | 🔴 |
| Agent runtime (copilot/claude) | ✅ inject | n/a | 🔴 twin | 🔴 |
| MCP (ADO/SharePoint) | 🔴 | n/a | 🔴 twin | 🔴 |

## Layers (sub-issues)
1. **CLI ↔ DTU seam** [cli] — configurable GitHub API base/auth so the CLI fetches from the Gitea adapter (hermetic) AND a GHE host (real enterprise). Keystone; unblocks the dress rehearsal (cli #56) and the real deployment.
2. **Full-loop deployment scenario** — actor mutates twin → CLI regenerates manifest from twin → app renders it → verify reflects the mutation. The end-to-end the real deployment IS.
3. **Work-graph DTU scenarios** — actor edits team.yaml/workstream.yaml or cuts a release → app reflects the new team/release node on refresh (extends issue-lifecycle/pr-and-merge to the org layer shipped in #232).
4. **Agent-runtime twin** [cli] — deterministic fake agent CLI so derive/generate fuzzy paths run hermetically in full-pipeline tests, not just unit injection.
5. **MCP server twins** [cli] — fake ADO board + SharePoint-docs MCP servers so MCP-preflight + derive against work-item/doc sources are exercised hermetically (the work-repo deployment's real dependencies).
6. **Visual-regression gate** — wire capture-review + BEAUTY.md into a baseline-diff check (per theme × surface), tied to twin states; catch visual regressions.
7. **TESTING.md — the pyramid + CI orchestration** — formalize what runs on PR (unit + static-twin fast gate) vs nightly (live DTU + full-loop + visual) vs exploratory; codify the holdout discipline across all twins.
8. **Exploratory-agent harness** — formalize the playbook: a scheduled/triggerable job that launches agent sessions against a running DTU to probe edge cases and open spec PRs (human-reviewed; assertions in specs, never in twins).

CLI-side layers (1, 4, 5) are tracked as issues in anokye-labs/kbexplorer-cli and linked here.

issues.title: Constellation legibility: orphan ring, unreadable labels at default zoom, duplicated legend
issues.body: Standard-of-beauty wave-1 finding (#239, BEAUTY.md SS4 finding 4, Graph: 2). Disconnected nodes ring the layout like noise (orphan ring); node labels are unreadable at default zoom; the in-canvas cluster legend duplicates the HUD cluster list. Explore: orphan shelf/cluster gutter instead of scatter, label LOD tied to zoom + degree, single source of truth for the legend. Relates to #53 (WebGL renderer) and #39 (rich graph views).

issues.title: Placeholder MAP minimap box renders empty on every reading surface
issues.body: Standard-of-beauty wave-1 finding (#239, BEAUTY.md SS4 finding 3, States: 2). The bottom-left minimap region renders as an empty bordered box labeled MAP on every reading/overview capture. Render the minimap content, lazy-render with a designed loading state, or remove the box until it has content. Principle 5: no placeholder ships.

issues.title: Theme-invariant accents: node icons and source badge keep dark palette on sepia/light
issues.body: Standard-of-beauty wave-1 finding (#239, BEAUTY.md SS4 finding 2, Theme: 2 / Color: 2). Cluster-colored node icons, the related-rail icons, and the 'Authored - <file>' source badge do not re-ramp per theme: on sepia the pale-blue badge on cream paper falls below readable contrast and the cold accents break the paper-and-ink treatment. Acceptance: per-theme accent ramps (or token-driven recolor) for node icons, rail icons, and badges; AA contrast verified on all three themes.

issues.title: Mobile HUD collapse failure: controls overlap title bar at 390px
issues.body:
Standard-of-beauty wave-1 finding (#239, BEAUTY.md SS4 finding 1, Responsive: 1). At 390x844 the bottom-dock controls (Theme/Dock/Aa/Width) overlap the node-title bar, the MAP button truncates at the left edge, and the RELATED rail collides with the controls panel. The HUD needs a mobile reflow: collapse to a single rail with expand-on-demand, or stack controls behind a sheet. Acceptance: no overlap/truncation at 390x844 in 
pm run capture:review output; touch targets >=40px.

issues.title: BEAUTY.md: the experiential quality standard, rubric, and wave-1 assessment
issues.body: Part of the standard-of-beauty epic #239. Deliverable: BEAUTY.md — principles, 0-4 scoring rubric across seven dimensions, review protocol (capture -> frontier-model image review -> scored assessment -> remediation issues), and the wave-1 assessment. Lands with the capture script PR.

issues.title: Bump uuid to 13.0.1 to fix Dependabot alert #7 (CVE-2026-41907)
issues.body:
## Summary

Dependabot alert [#7](https://github.com/anokye-labs/kbexplorer-template/security/dependabot/7) (moderate severity) flags `uuid@13.0.0` in `package-lock.json` — [GHSA-w5hq-g745-h8pq](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-w5hq-g745-h8pq) / CVE-2026-41907: missing buffer bounds check in `v3()`/`v5()`/`v6()` when a caller-provided `buf` is passed, allowing silent partial writes (CWE-787).

`uuid` is a transitive (peer) dependency of `vis-data`/`vis-network`. First patched version: **13.0.1**, which is within the existing `^13.0.0` peer range, so this is a lockfile-only bump.

## Plan

- Bump `uuid` to 13.0.1 in `package-lock.json` (`npm update uuid`)
- Run `npm test` and the build to confirm nothing breaks
- PR closes this issue and resolves the alert

issues.title: Canonical review screenshot capture across views, themes, and states
issues.body:
Part of the standard-of-beauty epic.

## What

A reproducible capture script (Playwright, building on the repo's existing visual-test machinery) that produces the canonical review surface set:

- Views: home/landing, constellation graph, reading view (long-form node), card grid/overview, HUD expanded + collapsed + docked variants, search palette (once it exists), source editor dialog.
- Themes: dark, light, sepia (+ at least one config-defined brand theme).
- States: cold load, node selected w/ neighborhood emphasis, cluster collapsed, detail-slider extremes.
- Output: `review/screenshots/<view>--<theme>--<state>.png` at 1440×900 and 390×844 (mobile), deterministic naming, one command (`npm run capture:review`).

These are review artifacts (gitignored or CI artifacts), not committed fixtures. The set definition lives in a small manifest file so the beauty review can enumerate coverage.

issues.title: Epic: Standard of beauty — agentic design review + experiential quality bar
issues.body:
## Why

kbexplorer's structural quality has gates (graph validation, assessment scoring, link health). Its **experiential quality has none** — nothing assesses whether the thing is beautiful: typography rhythm, color and contrast across themes, motion, graph readability, information hierarchy, the feel of moving resource-to-resource. For a sensemaking tool, beauty is not cosmetic; it is load-bearing — visual clarity IS comprehension.

This epic establishes a **standard of beauty**: an explicit, opinionated quality bar, an agentic review process that assesses the real rendered product against it (screenshots, not source), and a stream of driven improvements.

## Scope (sub-issues)
1. **Canonical screenshot capture** — reproducible script capturing the agreed surface set (all views × all themes × key states) for review input.
2. **BEAUTY.md — the standard** — the written bar: principles, per-surface criteria, scoring rubric, and the review protocol. Authored from an actual frontier-model design review of the captured surfaces, not invented in the abstract.
3. **Remediation wave 1** — issues filed from the first assessment, worked through the normal pipeline.

The standard then becomes a recurring gate: future UI PRs cite it, and periodic re-assessment keeps drift visible.

issues.title: Landing mode config: reading-first with collapsed graph
issues.body:
Part of the reader-first UX epic (Phase 2).

## What

A config-selectable landing experience that leads with content, not the constellation:

```yaml
# config.yaml
landing:
  view: reading        # reading | overview | graph (default today: graph/home)
  node: <id>           # optional: a specific node (e.g. the team home page); default = README/home node
  graph: collapsed     # HUD starts collapsed to its rail; one click expands
```

## Deliverables
- Config schema + wiring: initial route + HUD initial state honor the block; user preference (localStorage) wins after first interaction.
- The graph remains one gesture away: collapsed HUD shows the rail with the search button and an expand affordance.
- Deep links still work (hash routes unchanged).
- Tests: config parsing, initial-state logic, an E2E for "lands on reading view with collapsed HUD".

issues.title: Search: build-time index + HUD search button + Ctrl-K palette
issues.body:
Part of the reader-first UX epic (Phase 2). The single most-requested missing affordance: there is no search anywhere in kbexplorer.

## What

Client-side search over all nodes, served from a build-time index — no backend, consistent with the static secret-free architecture.

## Deliverables
- **Index**: built into the manifest (or a sibling `search-index.json`) at generate/build time — id, title, type, cluster, headings, body text (tokenized/trimmed). Runtime mode falls back to indexing loaded nodes in-memory. Use a tiny client lib (minisearch or comparable, license-compatible) or hand-rolled inverted index — justify the choice in the PR.
- **UI**: a search button in the HUD + global Ctrl-K (and `/`) command palette: type → ranked results (title match > heading > body) with type/cluster badges → Enter navigates to the node in reading view; arrow keys navigate results. Fluent v9 components, all three themes, keyboard-trap-free, accessible (combobox/listbox semantics).
- Works in both local-manifest and runtime-GitHub modes.
- E2E coverage (Playwright) for open-search→type→navigate, plus unit tests for ranking.
- Result cap + perf budget: index build adds <2s to build; palette opens <100ms on a 500-node graph.

issues.title: Epic: Reader-first UX — search + content-first landing
issues.body:
## Why (Phase 2 of the work-repo deployment)

Feedback and the target UX agree: the graph must not be in people's faces. People should land on content, navigate resource-to-resource, and reach for the graph (collapsed at the side) and search when they need them. Search does not exist at all today.

## Scope (sub-issues)
1. **Search** — build-time index in the manifest + HUD search button + Ctrl-K command palette.
2. **Landing mode** — config to make reading view the landing experience with the graph collapsed into the HUD by default.

issues.title: Person nodes: first-class people aggregating their active work
issues.body:
Part of the work-graph vocabulary epic (Phase 1).

## What

People as first-class nodes. Today authors/assignees are strings on issue/PR nodes; coworker visibility ("what is Adwoa working on?") needs a person node aggregating: authored/assigned open PRs and issues, team membership (from team.yaml), and recent activity.

## Deliverables
- `person` node type; identity = GitHub login, displayName overridable by content-model person files.
- Derived edges: person → assigned/authored issues & PRs (from existing work data — no new API calls), person → team (when descriptors exist).
- Synthesis rule: person nodes materialize when (a) a person descriptor exists, or (b) login appears as author/assignee on ≥1 active item — keep the graph from exploding with drive-by contributors (threshold/config).
- OrgChart provider enrichment optional, not required.
- Reading view: a person page listing their active work as navigable links.
- Tests.

issues.title: Release nodes: node type, edges to shipped PRs/issues, reading view
issues.body:
Part of the work-graph vocabulary epic (Phase 1). Companion to the kbexplorer-cli release-ingestion feature.

## What

Release nodes in the graph: each GitHub release becomes a node (tag, name, date, notes summary) with edges to the PRs/issues it shipped (parsed from release notes references) and to the repository node.

## Deliverables
- `release` node type in the engine (types, WorkProvider or new provider path) consuming releases from the manifest (CLI side ingests via `gh release list` — see the cli issue) and from the GitHub API in runtime mode.
- Edges: release → repository; release → referenced PRs/issues (#N parsing, same approach as issue cross-references).
- Reading view renders release notes markdown; cluster/visual defaults ("Releases" lane).
- Layer filtering: releases belong to the Work view.
- Tests per existing provider test patterns.

issues.title: Work-graph entity schema: team/workstream/priority/person/system-of-record descriptors
issues.body:
Part of the work-graph vocabulary epic (Phase 1).

## What

Define and implement the YAML descriptor schema for organizational entities in the content-model engine (F2): `team`, `workstream`, `priority`, `person`, `system-of-record`.

## Deliverables

- **Schema proposal first**: a `docs/work-graph-vocabulary.md` (or content-model schema addition) PR with the YAML shapes + example files, reviewed before implementation. Example direction:

```yaml
# content-model/teams/graph-platform.yaml
kind: team
id: graph-platform
name: Graph Platform
members: [adwoa, kwame]
workstreams: [kb-explorer]
```

```yaml
# content-model/workstreams/kb-explorer.yaml
kind: workstream
id: kb-explorer
name: KB Explorer
priority: p1
team: graph-platform
systems-of-record:
  - { name: "ADO board", url: "https://..." }
```

- Content-model builder support: these kinds produce nodes + derived edges (member-of, owns, has-priority, tracked-in), with the same source-of-truth editability PR #205 gave entity files (the `sourceFile` affordance should light up on them).
- Validation with actionable errors (unknown kind, dangling references) surfaced through the existing graph-validation gate.
- Cluster/visual defaults so the organizational layer reads as its own region of the graph.
- Hermetic tests following the content-model builder test patterns.

## Non-goals
Release ingestion (separate sub-issue), live person-activity aggregation (person nodes sub-issue).

issues.title: Epic: Work-graph vocabulary — teams, workstreams, priorities, releases, people
issues.body:
## Why (Phase 1 of the work-repo deployment)

The target deployment is a work repository where people need sensemaking over **active PRs, work items, releases, workstreams, priorities, and what coworkers are doing**. Issues/PRs/commits/branches already ingest, but the *organizational layer* — the thing that turns repo activity into a navigable map of work — has no vocabulary: no team, workstream, priority, release, person, or system-of-record node types.

The F2 content-model pipeline (schema-driven YAML/JSON entity files under `content-model/`, Epic #147) is exactly the right substrate. The host work repo will enforce consistency with YAML descriptor files; those descriptors ARE the contract this epic defines.

## Outcome

Drop `team.yaml` / `workstream.yaml` / release data into a repo and the graph grows an organizational layer: a workstream node links to its priority, its team, its active PRs and issues, its releases; a person node aggregates their authored/assigned work. Resource-first navigation works across it (click a teammate → their workstream → its open PRs).

## Scope (sub-issues)

1. **Work-graph entity schema** — YAML descriptor shapes for `team`, `workstream`, `priority`, `person`, `system-of-record` in the content-model engine, with derived edges (member-of, owns, prioritized-as, tracked-in).
2. **Release nodes** — ingestion in kbexplorer-cli (`gh release list` → manifest) + release node type + edges to PRs/tags here.
3. **Person nodes** — promote people from author/assignee strings to first-class nodes aggregating their active work, optionally enriched by the existing OrgChart provider.

issues.title: scripts/generate-manifest.js ignores VITE_KB_HOST_ROOT in vendored installs
issues.body:
## Repro

In a host repo using `kbexplorer init --vendor` (so `.kbexplorer/` lives one level deep inside the host, not as a git submodule):

`
node .kbexplorer/scripts/generate-manifest.js
`

writes a manifest containing the **template's stock content** (37 files starting with `content/app-shell.md`, README `# kbexplorer-template`) rather than the host repo's authored content.

## Cause

`detectHostRoot()` resolves `kbRoot/../..`, which only works for git-submodule layouts (where `.kbexplorer` is two levels deep). In vendored mode that path lands **above** the host repo, the lookup fails, and the script falls back to treating `kbRoot` as the host.

The companion CLI (`anokye-labs/kbexplorer-cli`) already passes `VITE_KB_HOST_ROOT=<host>` via env on dev/build, but this script never reads it.

## Suggested fix

At the top of the script:

`js
const hostRoot = process.env.VITE_KB_HOST_ROOT
  ? resolve(process.env.VITE_KB_HOST_ROOT)
  : detectHostRoot();
`

Falls back to existing behavior for standalone use; honors the explicit env var when the CLI provides it.

## Impact

Until this is fixed, `kbexplorer dev` in a vendored install renders the template's own knowledge base instead of the user's. Discovered while dogfooding kbexplorer on the CLI repo itself.

issues.title: Epic: External theme & branding customization (no submodule edits)
issues.body:
## What
kbexplorer themes are hardcoded in the `.kbexplorer` submodule
(`src/hooks/useTheme.ts`: `THEME_MAP` / `MODES` / the sepia `createLightTheme`
build). Move customization OUT of the submodule so host repos can restyle
colors, fonts, per-page/per-cluster accents, logos, and favicons — primarily via
the `config.yaml` that `parser.ts → loadConfig()` already fetches from the host
repo at runtime.

## Why
Today any restyle requires editing the submodule. Two `theme` fields
(`theme.default`, `theme.font.*`) are already declared in the type +
`DEFAULT_CONFIG` but nothing reads them — the promise exists but is unwired.

## Adopted model / approach
- Transport: `config.yaml theme:` (Option A) is the backbone; dedicated theme
  files (B), raw CSS (C) and JS module (D) are later substitutes/escape hatches.
- Scope axis: global → per-cluster → per-page, always as TOKEN DELTAS layered on
  the active base theme (dark/light/sepia) — never a full theme replacement, so
  the global theme switcher keeps working.
- Assets (logos/favicons) are orthogonal URL refs resolved through the existing
  `resolveImageUrl(source, …)` host-repo path.
- Start simple and grow: 5 phases, each shippable independently.

## Scope boundaries
- In: F1–F5 below (config schema, dynamic theme build, branding assets, scope
  layer, modularization).
- Out: redesigning the visual system / node renderer; theming the vis-network
  canvas internals beyond existing `isDark` usage.

## Success definition
A host repo can change global colors+fonts, set a logo and favicon, and accent
specific clusters/pages from its own `config.yaml` (+ optional assets), with NO
edits to the `.kbexplorer` submodule, verified live via Playwright.

## Children
Features F1–F5 below.

issues.title: F10 — Knowledge-base content refresh for the new node-type engine
issues.body:
## What
Refresh the kbexplorer **authored knowledge-base content** (`content/*.md`) so it documents the open, data-driven node-type engine and **all** the new node types now in the graph. Today only `content/node-types.md` (F1 foundation) is current; the content-model ingestion pipeline (F2), the `.github` structural nodes (F3), the content-model **spine viewers** (Person / Squad / Workstream / Mission / Priority / Cycle / Org), and the new **skill** node type are undocumented in the wiki.

## Why
The wiki is itself a kbexplorer graph; it should reflect the system it ships. New contributors — and the graph's own self-description — currently can't discover how nodes are typed, ingested, or rendered. The engine code, tests, and a sample `content-model/` exist; the authored content has not caught up.

## Scope (pages)
- [ ] **content-model-ingestion.md** — the 5-pass `ContentModelProvider` (schema reader -> discovery -> node emission -> edge resolution -> assembly), `@type`-driven kind (never path), URN/CURIE resolution, safe no-op behavior, and the build wiring (`generate-manifest.js` -> `manifest.contentModel`).
- [ ] **structural-nodes.md** — `StructuralProvider`: `.github` workflows / actions / issue+PR templates / CODEOWNERS / dependabot / funding **plus the new `skill` (`SKILL.md`) node**, each linked to the `repo-meta` repository node via `structural` edges; the bespoke viewers (WorkflowView / ActionView / SkillView / GenericStructuredView).
- [ ] **Update `node-types.md` + `ui-node-types.md`** — enumerate the full registry: person, squad, workstream, mission, priority, cycle, org, workflow, github-action, skill, dependabot/funding/codeowners/templates. Explain the viewer registry keyed by `@type` and the open `NodeSource`/`DisplayMode` unions.
- [ ] Wire `connections:` frontmatter so the new pages join the **engine** cluster graph (no orphan nodes; every node within 3 hops of the hub).
- [ ] A short **sample content-model** note pointing at the committed `content-model/` starter directory.

## Approach
Use the kb content pipeline (`/kb:generate` -> kb-architect -> kb-writer) or author directly. Keep frontmatter native (id/title/emoji/cluster/connections). Dark-mode Mermaid for the pipeline diagrams.

## Acceptance / Evidence
- New pages render as nodes in the running app (local mode), within 3 hops of the hub, no orphans (`npm run validate` passes).
- Screenshots of the `content-model-ingestion` and `structural-nodes` pages rendered through the reading view.
- `tsc -b` = 0, `npm run lint` = 0 errors, `vitest` green, `vite build` green.

---
Relates to Epic #147 (E1). Follows F1 #148 / F2 #149 / F3 #150. The `skill` node type + a sample `content-model/` landed on branch `hoopsomuah/explore-node-types`.

issues.title: Bug: Baseline tsc/lint debt on main (blocks release readiness)

## What

## Why
F4 (#151) is "Integration validation & **release readiness**." A repo whose typecheck and lint gates are red cannot honestly claim release readiness, and every downstream Feature (F2/F3) inherits a red baseline, making "is it my change or pre-existing?" triage harder. This is real debt that should be burned down on a `main` that already includes the F1 foundation.

## Scope
- Make `npx tsc -b` exit 0 across the repo (fix or correctly suppress the ~52 errors; add `@types/node` to the test tsconfig if that is the right fix).
- Make `npm run lint` exit 0 (~40 errors: unused imports, enum/erasableSyntaxOnly, etc.).
- Do NOT change runtime behavior; this is hygiene only.

## Validation
- `npx tsc -b` exits 0.
- `npm run lint` exits 0.
- `npm test` (vitest) and `npx vite build` remain green (no regressions).

## Evidence
- Paste before/after error counts for both `tsc -b` and `lint`.
- CI `test` check green on the PR.

Relates to PR #171. Blocks F4 (#151).

**Parent epic:** E1 — Open, data-driven node-type engine

## What

## Why
This is how the engine **becomes the model**. With the source repo sunset, the engine must build the graph from entity files itself. Doing it schema-driven (URN bases from `context.jsonld`, kind from `@type`, storage from `conventions.yaml`, relationships from `edges.yaml`) means a second org/repo adopts the platform by changing config — not engine code.

## Approach / key files
- `src/engine/content-model/` — schema reader + builder.
- `src/engine/providers/content-model-provider.ts` — discovery + node emission + edge resolution.
- `src/engine/remote-loader.ts` / `local-loader.ts` — register the provider.
- `scripts/generate-manifest.js` — build-time assembly path for the heavy multi-hundred-file walk (recommended default).
- `src/views/viewers/` — per-kind spine viewers.

## Acceptance summary
A fixture content tree (identity + schema + a handful of entity files) builds into a graph whose nodes carry correct `@id`/`@type`/`data`, whose edges carry the six-relation taxonomy, and whose unresolved FKs become stub nodes. Person and Squad render via bespoke viewers.

issues.title: Epic: Open, data-driven node-type engine for kbexplorer-template
issues.body:
## What
Replace kbexplorer-template's **closed, compile-time** node-type system — hardcoded `NodeSource` / `DisplayMode` / `EdgeType` unions, a `renderContent` switch, and bespoke per-source providers — with an **open, data-driven** one:

- **JSON-LD node internals** (`@id` / `@type` / typed `data`) on `KBNode`.
- A **node-type registry** that declares each type's discovery, mapping, cluster, layer, relations, and viewer in one place.
- A **viewer registry keyed by `@type`** with a generic structured fallback (total coverage; bespoke viewers are additive).
- **Schema-driven content-model ingestion** that builds the graph from entity files (the model documented in `content-model.md`).
- **Repo-structural discovery**: `.github` workflows, Actions, and templates become nodes linked to the repository node.

## Why
The originating content-model repo (Xbox Personalization) is being **sunset**. kbexplorer-template must become the new system of record and **own the files→graph pipeline itself** — no dependency on an externally pre-built `graph.json`. Migration will surface new node kinds (squad/cell/crew, sprint/cycle/season, …) that must be absorbed by **configuration, not core surgery**. Repo structure should be first-class graph citizens. JSON-LD + a viewer registry is the smallest durable abstraction that delivers the originally requested Person / Squad / Team views *and* scales to arbitrary structured knowledge.

## Adopted model
We adopt the proven three-layer model from `content-model.md`: **identity** (`teamops.yaml` → `kg://` URN authority/org) → **shape** (`schema/conventions.yaml`, `edges.yaml`, `lifecycle.yaml`, `entities/*.schema.json`, `index/context.jsonld`) → **content** (one file per entity). URN = JSON-LD `@id`; kind = `@type` (never inferred from path); `edges.yaml` is the relationship manifest; a 5-pass builder walks files → resolves edges → derives → clusters → stubs unresolved targets.

## Scope boundaries
- In: the engine (types, registries, providers, viewers, loaders, manifest build).
- Out (tracked as backlog Features F5/F6 and Epic 2): editor→PR write-back, cross-repo `@context` synonym mapping, fuzzy/docx derivation, unattended CI.

## Success definition
On **real content**, a Person node and a Squad node render via bespoke viewers, an arbitrary structured file renders via the generic fallback, and a `.github` workflow appears as a node edged to the repository node — all **without editing core unions** to introduce a new kind.

## Children
Features F1–F6 (below). **Relates to** Epic 2 (`anokye-labs/kbexplorer-cli`) which produces the fuzzy/docx-derived JSON-LD this engine ingests.

issues.title: Evaluate WebGL graph renderer to replace vis-network at scale
issues.body:
## Problem

vis-network struggles with our current graph size (~150+ nodes, ~250+ edges). Layout stabilization is slow, rendering is jittery, and we're not yet at the scale the provider system will produce. The graph provider architecture will generate 1000+ nodes with 5000+ edges.

## Research Summary

| Library | Rendering | Max Nodes | Custom Shapes | React | Status |
|---------|-----------|-----------|---------------|-------|--------|
| **Sigma.js** | WebGL | 10k+ | Yes (plugins) | Wrappers | Active (v3, paired with Graphology) |
| **react-force-graph** | WebGL (Three.js) | 10k+ | Yes | Native React | Active |
| **Cosmos** | GPU (WebGL/WebGPU) | 10k+ | Limited | Unknown | Emerging |
| **G6 (AntV)** | Canvas | ~10k | Yes (high) | Via Graphin | Active |
| **Cytoscape.js** | Canvas | <10k | Yes | Manual | Active but canvas-bound |

## Top Candidates

### Sigma.js + Graphology
- Best 2D WebGL option for 10k+ nodes
- Graphology handles graph data structure, Sigma renders
- Custom node programs (WebGL shaders) for shapes
- Force-directed via ForceAtlas2 (same algorithm we use now)
- Active v3 with modern API

### react-force-graph
- Native React component, WebGL via Three.js
- 2D and 3D modes
- Best for React integration
- Force-directed only (d3-force)
- Comprehensive styling

### Cosmos
- Full GPU simulation AND rendering
- Fastest at extreme scale
- Limited styling (no custom node shapes yet)
- Newest, least proven

## What We Need from a Replacement

- [ ] Custom node shapes (rounded rects with SVG/icon inside)
- [ ] Typed edge styling (different colors, dash patterns, arrows per edge type)
- [ ] Click-to-navigate on nodes
- [ ] Zoom/pan with controls
- [ ] Emphasize/dim nodes (active node + neighbors highlighted)
- [ ] Force-directed layout that stabilizes and stops
- [ ] Handle 5k+ nodes at interactive FPS
- [ ] Reasonable bundle size

## Recommendation

Evaluate **Sigma.js + Graphology** first — it matches our existing ForceAtlas2 layout, has WebGL rendering, supports custom node programs, and the Graphology data structure aligns well with our typed edge model. If custom node rendering is too limited, fall back to **react-force-graph**.

## Migration Path

1. Prototype: render current graph data with Sigma.js in the overlay
2. Compare: side-by-side performance at current node count
3. If good: migrate sidebar graph and minimap
4. If not: try react-force-graph

issues.title: Edge-type-aware related panel ranking
issues.body:
## Problem

The Related panel in the HUD shows the top 8 neighbors sorted by degree (connection count). This pushes out file nodes and other low-degree nodes, even when they have strong typed edges to the current node.

For example, `content-pipeline` has a `derived_from` edge (weight 3.0) to its source file `file-content/content-pipeline.md` and a `references` edge (weight 2.0) to `file-src/engine/parser.ts` — but neither appears in the Related panel because authored nodes with more connections rank higher by raw degree.

## Expected

The Related panel should rank by **edge weight × relevance**, not just neighbor degree. A `derived_from` edge (weight 5.0) should rank higher than a `mentions` edge (weight 0.5), regardless of the target node's degree.

## Proposed Ranking

`score = edge_weight * (1 + target_degree * 0.1)`

This preserves the preference for well-connected nodes but lets strong edges (contains, derived_from, imports) compete with high-degree-but-weakly-connected nodes.

## Additional: Group by Edge Type

Consider grouping the Related panel by edge type:

\\\
Source File
  content-pipeline.md (derived from)

References
  src/engine/parser.ts
  src/api/github.ts

Related Architecture
  Graph Engine (frontmatter)
  Type System (frontmatter)
\\\

This gives the user a structured view of different relationship types instead of a flat list.

## Verified via Playwright

`content-pipeline` has 2 file edges in the data but 0 file nodes in the Related panel — all 8 slots taken by higher-degree authored nodes.

issues.title: Clickable file path references in reading view
issues.body:
## Problem

The user sees code-formatted text but can't navigate to the file node.

File path mentions that have corresponding `file-*` nodes in the graph should render as clickable links in the reading view, navigating to `#/node/file-src/engine/parser.ts`.

## Verified via Playwright

Edge exists in data:
`content-pipeline → file-src/engine/parser.ts` (type: references)
But renders as plain code text, not a navigable link.

issues.title: Inline link extraction — connections derived from content, not frontmatter
issues.body:
## Content Node

See `content/spec-inline-link-extraction.md` in the knowledge graph for the full design.

## Core Principle

**Inline links ARE the graph edges.** A markdown link `[Graph Engine](graph-engine)` in the body should automatically create an edge. No frontmatter duplication.

## Why This Matters

1. **Duplication** — same relationship stated in body + frontmatter
2. **Staleness** — remove inline link, frontmatter persists
3. **Lost precision** — frontmatter is document-level; inline links carry section location
4. **Split breakage** — 1-to-N splitting puts frontmatter connections on parent, but inline links stay with their section

## Link Types

- Markdown: `[text](target)`
- Issue refs: `#N`
- Code imports: `import { x } from './file'`
- File containment: directory → file
- Git: commit → file

## Impact

- Frontmatter `connections:` becomes optional/supplementary
- `links` command changes: 'missing ref' means 'mention without link' not 'missing frontmatter'
- Edges carry `location` (line, section) for correct 1-to-N splitting

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Markdown `[text](target)` links auto-create edges
- [ ] Issue `#N` refs auto-create edges (already partial)
- [ ] Edges carry source type: inline, frontmatter, or inferred
- [ ] Edges carry location (line number, section heading)
- [ ] 1-to-N splitting assigns inline edges to correct section nodes
- [ ] `links` command suggests converting mentions to inline links
- [ ] Frontmatter connections that duplicate inline links are flagged

issues.title: Replace GitHub API with local data for self-exploration
issues.body:
## Problem

kbexplorer fetches ALL content via GitHub API at runtime — authored markdown, file tree, README, issues, PRs, commits, and config.yaml. This causes rate limiting (60 req/hr unauthenticated) and is wasteful for self-exploration where content is on disk.

## Solution: Manifest-Only Local Mode

A pre-build script generates a single `src/generated/repo-manifest.json` containing:
- **Authored content**: markdown files from `content/` read from disk
- **Config**: `config.yaml` parsed from disk
- **File tree**: local file system walk
- **README**: read from disk
- **Issues, PRs, commits**: fetched via `gh` CLI at build time (best-effort)

The app imports this manifest in local mode — zero API calls at runtime. Remote mode (GitHub API) is preserved for deployed instances exploring other repos.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `npm run dev` loads with zero GitHub API calls in local mode
- [ ] Authored content hot-reloads are not needed (manifest regeneration on dev start is sufficient)
- [ ] Issues, PRs, commits appear when `gh` CLI is available
- [ ] Explorer still works when `gh` CLI is not available (tree + README + authored content only)
- [ ] Remote mode (`VITE_KB_LOCAL` unset, no manifest) works exactly as before
- [ ] Comprehensive unit and scenario tests pass

issues.title: Authored mode: markdown with YAML frontmatter
issues.body:
## Overview

While the default experience uses GitHub API data (#12), kbexplorer also supports an **authored mode** where content comes from a collection of Markdown files with YAML frontmatter. This mode is designed for curated knowledge bases — design systems, architecture decision records, learning curricula, or team wikis.

### Frontmatter Schema

Each `.md` file declares its metadata in YAML frontmatter:

`yaml
---
title: Authentication Architecture
cluster: security
emoji: 🔐
sprite: /images/auth-icon.png
hero: /images/auth-hero.jpg
connections:
  - id: session-management
    type: references
  - id: oauth-flow
    type: depends-on
tags: [architecture, security, phase-1]
---
`

The engine parses these files using `gray-matter`, builds the graph from explicit `connections` arrays, and assigns visuals based on the mode selected (#9).

### Rendering

All prose is rendered using Fluent tokens for typography and colors. The default font is **Segoe UI** (via `tokens.fontFamilyBase`) for body text and headings. Code blocks use **Cascadia Code** (via `tokens.fontFamilyMonospace`). Colors, spacing, and radii all come from Fluent tokens through `makeStyles` — no custom CSS variables or hardcoded values.

### Clustering

In authored mode, clusters come from the `cluster` field rather than GitHub labels. This gives authors explicit control over how nodes group in the overview grid and the constellation graph (#10). The same cluster colors and visual indicators carry through the HUD (#11) and reading view connections sidebar.

### When to Use Which Mode

- **Repo-aware** (default): Zero-config exploration of any GitHub repo. Great for project onboarding. PRs are filtered out — only issues, README, and directory structure become nodes.
- **Authored**: Curated, designed knowledge experiences. Requires content creation but offers full control over structure, visuals, and narrative flow.

issues.title: Phase 2: Embedded Copilot conversation module
issues.body:
## Vision

Phase 2 introduces an embedded **GitHub Copilot conversation panel** directly inside kbexplorer. Users will be able to ask questions about the knowledge base — "What issues are related to authentication?", "Summarize the architecture decisions", "What's blocking the next release?" — and receive contextual answers grounded in the loaded graph data.

### How It Would Work

1. A collapsible chat panel slides in from the right side of the reading view, hosted inside a Fluent Dialog component for consistent overlay behavior
2. The conversation context includes the current node's content, its connections, and the full graph structure
3. Copilot generates responses using the knowledge graph as grounding — not generic answers, but answers specific to *this* repository's issues and structure
4. Responses can include clickable node references that navigate within kbexplorer

### Integration Points

- The HUD (#11) would gain a chat toggle Fluent Button in the right panel
- The graph view (#10) could support "find nodes about X" queries that highlight matching nodes
- The reading view would show inline suggestions for related content based on what you're reading
- The overview could offer a "summarize this cluster" action per cluster group
- All conversation UI would use Fluent components (Card, Button, Input, Body1, etc.) to match the existing design system

### Technical Approach

This would use the GitHub Copilot Extensions SDK to embed a Copilot-powered experience. The knowledge graph (#12) provides structured context that makes responses significantly more relevant than raw repository search. The Fluent theme system (#13) would style the chat panel automatically through FluentProvider context.

This is a Phase 2 feature — the current Phase 1 focuses on making the exploration experience excellent on its own (#9, #10, #11).

issues.title: Content from GitHub API: repo-aware mode
issues.body:
## Content from GitHub API

### Data Sources
- Fetches **issues**, **README**, and the **full file tree** from the GitHub API
- PRs and commits are **not** fetched — removed due to unreliable linking between PR nodes and the rest of the graph

### File Tree Processing
- Generates a **repo-root** node, **directory** nodes (2 levels deep), and individual **source file** nodes for `.ts`, `.tsx`, `.md`, `.json`, `.yaml`, and `.css` files
- Each file node is parented to its containing directory node

### README Handling
- README content is decoded with `TextDecoder` instead of `atob` to fix UTF-8 encoding issues with base64 content
- Content-based connections are created via keyword matching: a connection forms when 60% or more of a target node's title words appear in the README body
- `#N` issue references in the README also generate explicit connections

### Issue Processing
- Issues with 2 or more headings are split into a **parent** node plus individual **section** nodes

### Caching & Error Handling
- `CACHE_VERSION` constant enables cache versioning; stale data is auto-cleared on version bump
- An error screen is displayed when 0 nodes load (typically due to API rate limiting)

### Hub Node Selection
- The hub node (center of the graph) prefers the `readme` node; falls back to the highest-degree node

issues.title: HUD: Mukaase-inspired persistent control bar
issues.body:
## HUD

### Two Distinct Layouts
The HUD renders differently depending on dock position:

**Sidebar layout (left/right dock) — Okoto-inspired:**
- Top ~50%: live vis-network constellation graph
- Resizable split handle (row-resize cursor) between graph and connections list (range 20–80%)
- Connections list: cards showing icon + title + description + cluster color bar
- Compact tools strip at the bottom: theme toggle, dock selector, Aa font-size slider, Width slider

**Horizontal layout (top/bottom dock):**
- Minimap canvas
- Navigation row
- Related-nodes strip
- Tools panel

### Docking & Persistence
- Collapsible and dockable to 4 positions (top, bottom, left, right)
- Dock position and collapse state persisted in `localStorage`

### Sizing
- Sidebar width: **25vw** default, resizable from 15vw to 50vw via a drag handle
- Graph/connections split: **50%** default, resizable from 20% to 80% via the row-resize handle

### Constellation Overlay
- Full-screen overlay triggered by the MAP button
- Floating legend card showing cluster colors and counts
- Opens with a scale-out animation

issues.title: Constellation Graph: vis-network integration
issues.body:
## Constellation Graph

### Layout — No Separate Page
- There is no dedicated graph view page; the standalone route was removed entirely
- The constellation lives inside the **sidebar** (left/right dock) as a live vis-network instance
- A full-screen **overlay** is available via the MAP button, with a floating legend card and a scale-out open animation

### Sidebar Graph Behavior
- Sidebar graph uses smaller nodes (size range 28–44)
- Physics engine freezes after initial stabilization to keep the layout stable during interaction
- **Node emphasis:** the current node and its immediate neighbors render at full opacity; all other nodes fade to 30%

### Pan & Stabilization
- **Bounded panning:** a custom pointer-based pan handler clamps movement to the node bounding box, preventing the user from scrolling into empty space
- **Stabilization settings:** 150 iterations with `updateInterval: 150` — the graph renders once after settling rather than animating every intermediate frame

### Shared Infrastructure
- `createGraphNetwork()` factory in `src/engine/createGraphNetwork.ts` is shared by both the sidebar instance and the overlay instance

### Custom Node Shapes
- vis-network nodes use custom shapes via `ctxRenderer`: circles, rounded squares, and rounded rectangles
- Opaque node backgrounds prevent edges from showing through the node fill
- Disconnected nodes display a red **!** badge to flag orphan state

### Component Architecture
- `NodeVisual` component accepts a `clusterColor` prop for consistent color theming
- The 7 cluster surfaces still apply for UI chrome, but graph nodes bypass `NodeVisual` and use the custom canvas renderer directly

Sourced from @​playwright/test's releases.

v1.61.1

Bug Fixes

  • #41365 [Bug]: Expect.Extend matcher with same name as default matcher in same expect instance overrides default matchers implementation to custom matcher
  • #41351 [Bug]: Playwright UI mode: apiRequestContext._wrapApiCall reports unexpected number of bytes (same test passes in headed mode)

  • #41311 [Bug]: [Regression]: Sync loader throws "context.conditions?.includes is not a function" on Node 22.15
  • #41371 [Regression]: Sync ESM loader (registerHooks) fails to resolve extensionless .ts subpath imports across pnpm workspace symlinks

v1.61.0

🔑 WebAuthn passkeys

New Credentials virtual authenticator, available via browserContext.credentials, lets tests register passkeys and answer navigator.credentials.create() / navigator.credentials.get() ceremonies in the page — no real hardware key required, works in all browsers:

const context = await browser.newContext();

// Seed a passkey your backend provisioned for a test user.
await context.credentials.create('example.com', {
id: credentialId,
userHandle,
privateKey,
publicKey,
});
await context.credentials.install();


const page = await context.newPage();
await page.goto('https://example.com/login');
// The page's navigator.credentials.get() is answered with the seeded passkey.

You can also let the app register a passkey once in a setup test, read it back with credentials.get(), and seed it into later tests — see Credentials for details.

New WebStorage API, available via page.localStorage and page.sessionStorage, reads and writes the page's storage for the current origin:

await page.localStorage.setItem('token', 'abc');
const token = await page.localStorage.getItem('token');
const items = await page.sessionStorage.items();

New APIs

Network

  • apiResponse.securityDetails() and apiResponse.serverAddr() mirror the browser-side response.securityDetails() and response.serverAddr().
