pullRequests.body:
Bumps [@playwright/test](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright) from 1.60.0 to 1.61.0.
Release notes

Sourced from @​playwright/test's releases.

v1.61.0

🔑 WebAuthn passkeys

New Credentials virtual authenticator, available via browserContext.credentials, lets tests register passkeys and answer navigator.credentials.create() / navigator.credentials.get() ceremonies in the page — no real hardware key required, works in all browsers:

const context = await browser.newContext();

// Seed a passkey your backend provisioned for a test user.

await context.credentials.create('example.com', {

id: credentialId,

userHandle,

privateKey,

publicKey,

});

await context.credentials.install();


const page = await context.newPage();

await page.goto('https://example.com/login');

// The page's navigator.credentials.get() is answered with the seeded passkey.

You can also let the app register a passkey once in a setup test, read it back with credentials.get(), and seed it into later tests — see Credentials for details.

🗃️ Web Storage

New WebStorage API, available via page.localStorage and page.sessionStorage, reads and writes the page's storage for the current origin:

await page.localStorage.setItem('token', 'abc');
const token = await page.localStorage.getItem('token');
const items = await page.sessionStorage.items();

New APIs

Network

  • apiResponse.securityDetails() and apiResponse.serverAddr() mirror the browser-side response.securityDetails() and response.serverAddr().

Browser and Screencast

  • New option artifactsDir in browserType.connectOverCDP() controls where artifacts such as traces and downloads are stored when attached to an existing browser.
  • New option cursor in screencast.showActions() controls the cursor decoration rendered for pointer actions.
  • The onFrame callback in screencast.start() now receives a timestamp of when the frame was presented by the browser.

Test runner

  • The testOptions.video option now supports the same set of modes as trace: new 'on-all-retries', 'retain-on-first-failure' and 'retain-on-failure-and-retries' values. See the video modes table for which runs are recorded and kept in each mode.
  • Supported expect.soft.poll(...).
  • New fullConfig.argv — a snapshot of process.argv from the runner process, handy for reading custom arguments passed after the -- separator.
  • New fullConfig.failOnFlakyTests mirrors the config option, so reporters can explain why a flaky run failed.
  • testInfo.errors now lists each sub-error of an AggregateError as a separate entry.

pullRequests.title: Feature H: First-class service + decision kinds (viewers + edge rules)
pullRequests.body:
Implements **Feature H** (issue #275, under Epic #273): first-class service and decision content-model kinds with bespoke viewers and schema-driven edge rules — no core union edits (open node-type + viewer registries).

## What changed
- **register.ts** — registers service (relations: owned-by, tracked-in → `ServiceView`) and decision (relations: decided-by, affects → `DecisionView`), bound via `registerContentModelTypes()`.
- **ServiceView.tsx** — renders owning team, ServiceTree id (as a catalog link), `catalog-info` path, and repo path (link). className-styled, SSR-safe.
- **DecisionView.tsx** — renders deciders, a status pill, context, affected work, and consequences.
- **edges.yaml** (real + fixture):
  - `service.team` → team (`owned-by`)
  - `service.systems-of-record` → system-of-record (`tracked-in`)
  - `decision.deciders` → person (`decided-by`)
  - `decision.affects-workstreams` / `affects-missions` → workstream / mission (`affects`) — two fields because an FK rule has a single target kind.
- **conventions / lifecycle / context** updated for both kinds (service → `durable`, decision → `per-event`; both authority-scoped).
- Example entities under `content-model/services/` and `content-model/decisions/` that resolve cleanly.
- Bump `CACHE_VERSION` 31 → 32 (new kinds/entities change produced nodes).

## Tests / verification
- `vitest`: full suite **640 passing**, including new ServiceView/DecisionView render tests, extended registration resolution, and a new `service-decision` builder suite proving every FK resolves with no `unresolved-ref` on the happy path.
- `npm run build` (tsc -b + vite) passes; changed files lint clean (pre-existing lint findings in untouched HUD/NodeVisual/SearchPalette are baseline).
- Playwright (production preview): a **service node renders ownership + ServiceTree/catalog/repo links**; a **decision node renders deciders + context**.

Closes #275

pullRequests.title: feat(graph): reports-to org tree layout (#279)
pullRequests.body:
## Summary

Implements **Task C2 (#279)** — a hierarchical **reports-to tree layout** for the person graph that scales to a hundreds-person org. Additive and SSR-safe; the existing force layout is unchanged.

Selecting the new **Org** view projects the graph down to the reporting hierarchy and renders it as a top-down tree (managers above their reports), keyed on the `person-manager → reports-to` FK edge already defined in `content-model/schema/edges.yaml`.

## What changed
- **`src/engine/reports-to-layout.ts`** (new, pure, SSR-safe): `computeReportsToLevels` (BFS from roots, cycle-safe, multi-root, shortest-depth for multi-manager, O(V+E)), `projectReportsToTree` (person→person reporting subgraph + cap with breadth-first truncation), plus `selectReportsToEdges` / `hasReportsToTree` / `countReportsToParticipants` helpers.
- **`src/types/index.ts`**: `GraphView` gains an optional `layout` mode; new built-in **`org`** view requesting `reports-to`.
- **`src/engine/createGraphNetwork.ts`**: new `layout` option. In `reports-to` mode it assigns explicit vis-network `level`s, enables the hierarchical layout (UD), **disables physics** (deterministic + fast at scale), and reverses the *drawn* vis edges so managers sit above reports (semantic `KBEdge` direction is untouched). Viewport bounds / pan / zoom finalization refactored into an idempotent `finalizeLayout` driven by `requestAnimationFrame` + `afterDrawing` (the physics-off tree never fires `stabilized`).
- **`src/components/HUD.tsx`**: wires the active view's layout into the sidebar + overlay graphs; bypasses cluster-collapse and degree-trim for the org tree so the whole hierarchy renders, with an honest "showing N of M" count.
- **`src/engine/demo-entities.ts` / `useKnowledgeBase.ts`**: `?demo=bigorg` seam injects a deep/wide synthetic org (341 people) for scale validation.

## Design notes
Reviewed with a design critique before implementing. Key decisions: rely on **explicit `level` values** (not `sortMethod:'directed'`, which would invert the tree since edges are report→manager); **reverse only the rendered vis edges** for correct downward routing; **idempotent finalization** independent of physics lifecycle; deterministic ordering and cycle-safety for malformed org data.

## Verification
- `npm install`, `npm run build`, `vitest` (**641 tests pass**, incl. 20 new). `npm run lint` clean on all changed files (pre-existing repo lint debt in untouched `NodeVisual.tsx` / `SearchPalette.tsx` only).
- Playwright on `?demo=bigorg` + Org view: **341 person nodes**, **5 distinct tree levels**, root at top (UD), navigable via pan/zoom.

Closes #279

pullRequests.title: feat(person): navigable manager/team links in PersonView (#278)
pullRequests.body:
Closes #278

## What

Task C1 (Feature #274, Epic #273). `PersonView` rendered the **manager** (`Reports to`) and **team** field values as plain text. This makes them navigable graph links, reusing the existing `NodeLink` anchor (`#/node/<encoded id>`, with `data-node-id`).

## How

- New pure helpers in `spine-data.ts`:
  - `ldContextOf(node)` — reads the JSON-LD `@context` prefix -> URN-base map from the node's own envelope.

Returns `null` when unresolvable.
- `PersonView` gains a small `RefLink` component: renders `NodeLink` when `resolveRef` succeeds, else falls back to plain text (e.g. work-derived person nodes with no `@context`).
- SSR-safe, className-styled (no pixel sizing).

Extended `src/views/viewers/__tests__/spine-viewers.test.ts` with a `PersonView` block asserting manager id, team id, CURIE expansion, and the plain-text fallback (encoded href + data-node-id).

pullRequests.title: fix(manifest): host-root detection for vendored installs (#220)
pullRequests.body:
## What & why

Fixes #220. `scripts/generate-manifest.js` `detectHostRoot()` resolved `kbRoot/../..`, which only works for the **git-submodule** layout. For a **vendored** install (`.kbexplorer` one level deep inside the host repo) that lookup lands **above** the host repo, so the generated manifest captured the kbexplorer template's own stock content instead of the host repo's authored content.

## Change

Replaced the fixed-depth resolver with a data-driven `detectHostRoot(kbRootDir, env)`:

1. An explicit **`VITE_KB_HOST_ROOT`** env value always wins. This removes the need for the CLI's brittle string-patch of this script — host-root is now configuration, not a string-replaced line.
2. If the package is not the kbexplorer template, its own root is the host.
3. If the template is checked out standalone (dir not named `.kbexplorer`), there is no enclosing host — return its own root (prevents false positives in worktree/standalone dev).
4. Otherwise walk up from the install dir to the **nearest enclosing repo/package boundary** that is not the template itself. Handles **both** vendored and submodule layouts with no fixed depth assumption. `.git` is matched as file *or* dir (submodule-friendly), and ancestors whose `package.json` name is a template name (`kbexplorer` / `kbexplorer-template`) are skipped.

`detectHostRoot` is exported and parameterized so it is unit-testable; module-level behavior (`const hostRoot = detectHostRoot()`) is unchanged.

## Demonstration — vendored layout now reads host content

Fake vendored layout `my-host-repo/.kbexplorer/` with distinct READMEs:

```
kbRoot            : .../kb220demo/my-host-repo/.kbexplorer
OLD (../..)       : .../kb220demo                  => null            (escapes host; captures template stock)
NEW detectHostRoot: .../kb220demo/my-host-repo     => "# MY HOST REPO (authored content)"
ENV override      : C:/somewhere/else              (VITE_KB_HOST_ROOT honored)
```

## Tests

Added `detectHostRoot` coverage in `scripts/__tests__/generate-manifest.test.js`: explicit env override (+ blank-override ignored), vendored layout, submodule (deeper) layout, walking past a template-named ancestor, standalone checkout, and non-template root.

## Verification

- `npm install` — pass
- `npm run build` — pass
- `npm run lint` — the 6 errors / 4 warnings are **pre-existing** in `src/components/*` (identical on base via `git stash`); my changed files lint clean (`eslint scripts/...` exits 0)
- scripts vitest suite — **33 passed** (incl. 8 new `detectHostRoot` tests)

Closes #220

pullRequests.title: fix(graph): repair sensemaking — anchor work nodes to repo-meta, fold work cluster, tune visual density
pullRequests.body:
The deployed graph at [/#/node/home](https://anokye-labs.github.io/kbexplorer-template/#/node/home) had degraded sensemaking. This PR fixes the 3 issues called out + 6 more the new audits found, and adds **two CI-ready audits** so future regressions are caught before deploy.

## The 3 user-reported issues

1. **GitHub issues didn't link to their repository.** Every issue / PR / commit / non-default branch had _no_ typed edge to `repo-meta`. The graph relied on `#NNN` body refs alone — issues that didn't cross-reference others ended up disconnected.
2. **Repo node was floating alone.** `repo-meta` only declared `connections: [readme, default-branch]`. It was never a backlink target for issues/PRs/commits/releases. So the actual hub of the work graph was peripheral.
3. **Layout was unclean — nodes too big relative to text, edges hard to see.** The default `nodeSizeRange` was fixed (44–64) regardless of node count, and faded-edge alpha was `0.08`, effectively invisible on dark theme.

## Additional issues the audits caught

4. **Cluster proliferation: 28 → 13 → 12+1 hidden.** Each issue label became a top-level cluster (`Pull Request`, `Person`, `Squad`, `Workstream`, `Mission`, `ORG`, `Cycle`, …). The structural fix dropped this to 13; the visual audit then caught that 13 was still too many for the legend; the engine fold + legend cap brought it to 12 visible.
5. **569 phantom `#NNN` edges** to nonexistent issue/PR numbers from PR/release/commit bodies.
6. **`repo-meta` and `repo-root` were two separate disconnected nodes for the same repository.**
7. **276 nodes were unreachable from the actual hub** before orphan-rescue applied.
8. **13 genuine orphans** were rendered as floating circles with no label.
9. **1-hop neighbours of the focused node were unlabelled** at large graph sizes.

## Engine fixes

- **`parser.ts`** — `issueToNode` now takes `IssueToNodeOptions` (`knownIssueNumbers`, `knownPrNumbers`, `repoNodeId`):
  - forces every issue into the unified `work` cluster (labels become tags, not clusters)
  - filters `#NNN` refs to known issues/PRs only — no phantom edges
  - emits a typed `tracked-in` edge to `repo-meta` + sets `parent: 'repo-meta'`
  - file-tree nodes (`repo-root`, `dir-…`, `file-…`) now use the `infra` cluster instead of a separate `code` cluster (one fewer chip)
- **`work-provider.ts`** — same fixes for PRs, plus:
  - every branch is `tracked-in repo-meta` (was: default branch only)
  - commits summary node `tracked-in repo-meta`
  - `repo-meta` declares a `contains` edge to `repo-root` so the GitHub repo + file tree are one navigable cluster
  - PRs, commits, releases all now use the unified `work` cluster (no more `pull-request` / `commits` / `releases` chips)
- **`person-provider.ts`** — GH-derived person nodes now use the `work` cluster (content-model people keep their own `person` cluster — those are first-class authored entities)
- **`createGraphNetwork.ts`** — visual density tuning + audit hook:
  - **adaptive `nodeSizeRange`** based on graph size — >600 → [22,36], >200 → [28,44], >80 → [34,52], else [44,64]
  - **brighter faded-edge colour** for dark theme (`rgba(160,160,160,0.18)` was `rgba(80,80,80,0.08)`)
  - **1-hop neighbours of the focused node are always labelled** (`labelDegreeThreshold: 0` override)
  - new `auditSlot` option exposes the vis-network instance on `window.__kbeNetworks[slot]` and stamps an `__auditLabel` sidecar on each node so the visual audit can probe the live render
- **`HUD.tsx`** — legend cap with overflow chip:
  - cluster chips sorted by node count, top-12 shown, rest folded behind a single `"+N more"` chip (hover tooltip lists the hidden ones)
  - `data-kbe-legend="cluster"` / `"overflow"` / `"legend-root"` attributes so audits read rendered chip counts directly
- **`content/config.yaml`** — stable cluster colour definitions for `work`, `pull-request`, `commits`, `releases`, `person`, `code`, `docs` so legend colours are deterministic across the transition
- **`src/api/github.ts`** — bumped `CACHE_VERSION 29 → 30` (required for any graph-shape change per AGENTS.md)

## Audit infrastructure

The existing `kbx graph assess` only inspects authored markdown in `content/`. The runtime graph the user sees is much larger because it includes issues, PRs, commits, branches, structural `.github` files, and content-model entities. **Neither tool could catch what the user actually sees rendered.** So this PR adds two complementary audits.

### Runtime audit (data-shape contract)

**`scripts/audit-runtime-graph.mjs`** — loads `src/generated/repo-manifest.json`, simulates the graph the same way the runtime providers do, and reports:

- cluster proliferation
- unlinked issues / PRs
- repo-disconnection
- unreachable nodes (computed *before* orphan-rescue so the rescue doesn't hide structural gaps)
- genuine orphans
- tiny clusters
- low-degree nodes

Supports `--fail-on=ID,…` for CI gating. Runs in CI against the manifest the workflow already builds — no special tokens, no user auth.

### Visual audit (rendering contract) — **new in this iteration**

**`scripts/audit-visual.mjs`** — drives headless playwright against the built `local` mode and asserts six property-based checks against the *rendered* DOM + canvas:

| Check | What it verifies |
| --- | --- |
| `hud-related-links` | Related-nodes pane has the expected link density |
| `legend-cluster-count` | Legend shows ≤ 12 visible chips (matches UI cap) |
| `legend-overflow-size` | Hidden `+N more` chip folds ≤ 5 clusters |
| `map-canvas-non-blank` | Visible non-background pixels exist on the MAP overlay |
| `map-edge-visibility` | Mid-luminance band proves edges + labels actually paint (not just node fills) |
| `map-label-coverage` | ≥ 20% of in-viewport nodes carry text |
| `focus-neighbour-labels` | All 1-hop neighbours of the focused node are labelled |

The visual audit caught what the data-only audit missed: a structural fix that brought clusters from 28 → 6 in the manifest still produced **15 cluster chips in the rendered legend** because the live graph also includes content-model spine entities (priority / squad / workstream) that the structural simulator doesn't replay. Without the visual audit I would have shipped a "fixed" PR that still violated the user's sensemaking principle.

The audit ships with two `npm` scripts:
- `audit:visual` — verbose, non-blocking
- `audit:visual:strict` — fails the run on high-severity findings (CI-ready)

### Why two audits?

They cover different failure surfaces:

| Audit | Catches | Doesn't catch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Runtime | Engine invariants — repo-meta linkage, cluster IDs in data, reachability, phantom edges | Anything UI-side: legend cap, label rendering, canvas paint, focus override |
| Visual | UI invariants — what the rendered DOM/canvas actually shows | Engine bugs that don't surface visually in the focused-node path |

Together they bracket the failure modes that caused this regression class.

## Tests

- `parser.test.ts` — replaced "uses first label as cluster" with the unified-`work` + `tracked-in` + phantom-ref-filter behaviour
- `work-provider.test.ts` — issue node cluster updated to `'work'`
- `release-provider.test.ts` — release nodes folded into `'work'` (was `'releases'`)
- `person-provider.test.ts` — GH-derived person nodes folded into `'work'` (was `'person'`)

**All 621 unit/integration tests pass. Build is clean.** Lint warnings in files I didn't touch are unchanged.

## Before / after metrics

|                              | Before    | After             |
| ---------------------------- | --------- | ----------------- |
| Manifest clusters            | 28        | **6**             |
| Rendered legend chips        | 15        | **12 visible + 1 hidden** |
| Hub                          | `pr-140` deg 33 | **`repo-meta` deg 291** |
| Unreachable nodes from hub   | 276       | **0**             |
| Genuine orphans              | 13        | **0**             |
| Phantom `#NNN` edges         | 569       | **0**             |
| Issues linked to repo        | 0 / 85    | **85 / 85**       |
| PRs linked to repo           | 0 / 151   | **151 / 151**     |

## Workflow follow-up

The local copilot-CLI token doesn't have the `workflow` scope, so the `.github/workflows/github-pages.yml` update isn't in this push. Please add these steps so both audits gate the build:

```yaml
      - name: Audit runtime graph
        run: node scripts/audit-runtime-graph.mjs --fail-on=issues-not-linked-to-repo,prs-not-linked-to-repo,repo-meta-repo-root-disconnected,cluster-proliferation,unreachable-from-hub,genuine-orphans

      - name: Audit visual rendering
        run: |
          npx playwright install chromium
          node scripts/audit-visual.mjs --fail-on=legend-cluster-count,legend-overflow-size,map-edge-visibility,map-label-coverage,focus-neighbour-labels
```

## How to think about future degradations

The pattern that caused this: the engine has an **orphan-rescue** path that attaches degree-0 nodes to the highest-degree node with a weak `related` edge. That gives a false sense of connectivity, hiding real structural breaks. Each audit closes a different gap:

- **Runtime audit** computes reachability *before* rescue and tracks which kinds of nodes have typed vs inferred edges to the repo.
- **Visual audit** measures what the user actually sees — labels on focused-node neighbours, cluster chip count, edge visibility — because the structural data being correct doesn't guarantee the render is legible.

When you change a provider, ask: _do my new nodes get a typed edge to a structural anchor?_ When you change the HUD, ask: _are the cluster chips and labels still bounded as the graph grows?_ The audits answer both.

## What this adds

Formalises the exploratory-agent playbook (documented in `twins/gitea/README.md`) into a runnable, schedulable harness.

### `scripts/explore-dtu.mjs` + `npm run explore:dtu`

A script that:
1. Brings the Gitea DTU up (`dtu:up` → `dtu:seed`)
2. Starts the GitHub→Gitea adapter and the Vite app as background processes
3. Waits for both to pass their readiness checks
4. Prints a ready-to-paste probing prompt for the orchestrator / agent session
5. Optionally writes `.dtu/session-brief.json` (set `EXPLORE_WRITE_BRIEF=1` or runs automatically under CI)

**It does NOT call any LLM.** The harness stages the environment; the orchestrator reads the brief and launches the agent session externally. This boundary is documented clearly in the script header and in `docs/exploratory-agent.md`.

Env-var opt-outs: `EXPLORE_SKIP_DTU`, `EXPLORE_NO_APP`, `EXPLORE_WRITE_BRIEF`, `EXPLORE_ADAPTER_PORT`, `EXPLORE_APP_PORT`. Cross-platform safe (uses `npm.cmd` / `npm exec` for Vite invocation on Windows).

- Triggers: `workflow_dispatch` + weekly schedule (Monday 06:00 UTC)

Full reference: the loop diagram, env var table, CI workflow description, session-brief JSON schema, actor CLI examples, and spec-authoring guidelines for agent PRs.

pullRequests.title: feat(review): visual-regression gate + stable capture-report (drop bytes churn)
pullRequests.body:
Closes #257

## What this does

Three coordinated changes to turn the capture-review harness into a regression gate.

### 1. Drop `bytes` from `capture-report.json` (churn fix)

PNG compression is non-deterministic — byte counts changed on every capture run, causing repeated merge conflicts on the committed report. `bytes` is removed from both the script output (`scripts/capture-review.mjs`) and the committed file. Size-sanity is still verified internally (images < 5 KB are flagged as blank) but not persisted.

### 2. Visual-regression gate: `npm run verify:visual`

**Diff approach:** `pixelmatch` + `pngjs` (pixel-level perceptual diff).

| Decision | Choice | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| Tool | `pixelmatch` | Anti-aliasing-aware per-pixel diff; produces an inspectable diff PNG. Hash-only approaches (pHash/dHash) are compact but lose the diff image. |
| Baselines | Committed PNGs in `review/baselines/` | 64 images × ~80–230 KB ≈ 8 MB total. Acceptable repo weight; gives reviewers an exact visual reference. |
| Tolerance | `threshold: 0.1` per-channel | Allows sub-pixel AA variance between local/CI font rendering while catching real layout/color shifts. |
| Fail gate | `> 0.5%` differing pixels | Catches layout shifts and color regressions; ignores minor compression variance. |

`verify:visual` exits 0 on pass, 1 on failure. Diff images land in `review/diffs/` (gitignored) and are uploaded as CI artifacts.

**Bootstrap / update baselines:**
```sh
npm run capture:review -- --update-baselines
git add review/baselines
git commit -m "chore(review): update visual baselines"
```

### 3. Nightly/manual workflow (`.github/workflows/visual-regression.yml`)

`workflow_dispatch` + `schedule: 05:15 UTC`. **NOT wired into the fast PR gate** (`github-pages.yml`, `playwright.config.ts`) for three reasons:
- Captures need a full build + a real browser (~4–5 min)
- Screenshots are environment-sensitive (font rendering, GPU compositing)
- Baseline updates are deliberate commits, not auto-updates

## Verified locally

- `npm test`: 614 tests pass
- `npm run capture:review -- --update-baselines`: 64 captured, 8 skipped (source-editor, expected), baselines seeded
- `npm run verify:visual`: 64/64 pixel-perfect

pullRequests.title: test(dtu): Gitea live-twin multi-agent harness (Podman + tea)
pullRequests.body:
## What & why Adds a **stateful Digital Twin Universe (DTU)** that validates kbexplorer under realistic, *mutating* GitHub workflows — many actors create/edit issues, push branches, and open & merge PRs in a **real Gitea server**, and the app faithfully reflects those changes on refresh (including the cache‑TTL / ETag contract). This complements the existing **static** fixture twin (`twins/github/`) without touching it. A **GitHub‑REST → Gitea‑API translation proxy** sits on the unchanged `VITE_GH_API_BASE` seam, so the app stays byte‑for‑byte unchanged. ```mermaid flowchart LR ACTORS["Actors
tea CLI · REST helpers
scripted bots / agent sessions"] -->|create/edit issues · branches · PRs · merge| GITEA[("Gitea
Podman · SQLite")] GITEA --> ADAPTER["adapter.mjs
GitHub→Gitea proxy
ETag/304 · Link · X-RateLimit"] ADAPTER -->|GitHub REST v3| APP["kbexplorer app
remote/repo-aware mode"] PW["Playwright e2e"] --> APP PW --> ACTORS ``` ## Constraints honoured - **Podman, not Docker** — bootstrap starts the Podman machine when needed and runs a pinned `gitea/gitea` image; native on Linux CI (no VM). - **`tea`** (Gitea's `gh` analogue) is the actor CLI — auto‑downloaded/cached under gitignored `.dtu/bin/`. - **Zero secrets in the browser** — the admin token lives only in gitignored `.dtu/state.json` + process env and is used solely server‑side by the proxy. - **Purely additive / opt‑in** — the static twin and the fast e2e gate are untouched. The Gitea path is `npm run dtu:*` + `npm run test:e2e:gitea`, and CI is a scheduled/manual workflow, not the PR gate. ## What's inside - `twins/gitea/`: `bootstrap` · `seed` (working‑tree snapshot → twin `main` + baseline issues/PRs) · `adapter` (header synthesis, ETag/304, pagination, GitHub↔Gitea deltas) · `gitea-client` · `tea` provisioning · scripted `actors/*` · `teardown` · `global-setup.ts` · `README.md` (incl. **exploratory‑agent playbook**) · unit tests. - `e2e/gitea/`: `issue-lifecycle`, `pr-and-merge`, `adapter-refresh` scenario specs + `playwright.gitea.config.ts` (self‑contained globalSetup). - `adapter`: added GitHub‑faithful `X-RateLimit-Limit` header (+ unit coverage). - `gitea-client`: `mergePull` now waits for Gitea to compute mergeability before merging (fixes a 405 race). - Docs: `DTU.md` harness section; `.gitignore` for `.dtu/` + report dir. - Opt‑in `.github/workflows/dtu-gitea.yml` (nightly + `workflow_dispatch`). ## Verification - `npx tsc -b` → **0 errors** - `npm run lint` → **0 errors** (only the pre‑existing accepted `HUD.tsx` exhaustive‑deps warning) - `npx vitest run` → **491 passed** (incl. 22 adapter unit tests; +1 rate‑limit assertion) - `npm run test:e2e:gitea` → **5/5 passed** against live Podman Gitea: - adapter synthesizes GitHub headers, honors ETag→304, and a real mutation invalidates the cached representation - a newly opened issue surfaces as a node on a cache‑fresh load; a cached load hides it until refresh - an actor‑opened PR appears as a Pull Request node; merging a README edit updates the README node on `main` after refresh - `tea` CLI smoke: downloaded the binary, logged in against the twin, listed the twin's issues (including spec‑created ones) - **Live app loop:** the running app fetched issues/pulls/trees/contents from the twin and rendered **336 nodes / 341 connections**, with Bug/Enhancement/Documentation/Pull‑Request clusters reflecting seeded + actor‑created issues/PRs — zero console errors. Screenshots (home stats + overview reflecting the twin) captured during verification. > Note: this is the **testing harness** the orchestrator asked for as a precursor to landing F5 (PR #205, issue #152). It does not modify app behaviour and does not close #152.

pullRequests.body:
Bumps [yaml](https://github.com/eemeli/yaml) from 2.8.3 to 2.9.0.
Release notes

Sourced from yaml's releases.

v2.9.0

The changes here are really only patches, but I'm releasing this as a minor version to note a small change to the documentation of parseDocument() and parseAllDocuments(): I've removed the claim that they'll "never throw".

It remains the case that practically all non-malicious inputs will be handled without emitting an error, but there is a decent chance that code paths remain where e.g. a RangeError due to call stack exhaustion can be triggered by malicious inputs. Up to now, I've considered these as security vulnerabilities, and in fact it's the only category of error for which yaml CVEs have been issued so far.

Starting from this release, I'll be considering such errors as bugs, but not vulnerabilities. I do welcome people and/or LLMs looking for them, but please report them as normal issues rather than suspected security vulnerabilities. This also applies to previously undiscovered bugs in earlier releases.

  • fix: Avoid calling Array.prototype.push.apply() with large source array
  • fix(lexer): Avoid recursive calls that may exhaust the call stack

pullRequests.title: Add HUD theme palette chooser for all themes
pullRequests.body:
## What

The HUD previously exposed only three hardcoded **dark / light / sepia** buttons, so any config-defined, external-file, or JS-module theme was reachable **only** via the `t` keyboard cycle — with no visible affordance. This adds a clickable **paint-palette menu** in the HUD that lists *every* available theme.

## Changes

- **`useTheme.ts`** — now returns the live selectable mode list (`modesForMap(themeMap)`) as a 6th tuple element, so the UI knows the full dynamic set (built-ins + config + external-file + module themes).
- **`HUD.tsx`** — replaces the three fixed buttons with a Fluent `Menu` of `MenuItemRadio` items (one per theme), triggered by a `Color` palette-icon button. The active theme is checked; selection routes through `onThemeChange` (persisted to `kbe-theme`). Built-ins keep their moon/sun/book glyphs; named themes get a swatch icon and a title-cased label. `onThemeChange` widened from `Theme` to `ThemeMode`.
- **`App.tsx`** — threads `availableThemes` through to the HUD.
- **Docs** — `theming-named-themes.md` and `theming-overview.md` now describe the palette chooser alongside the `t` shortcut.

No cache/config-shape change, so `CACHE_VERSION` is unchanged (`kbe-theme` already existed).

## Validation

- `npx tsc -b` ✓, `npm run lint` 0 errors (only the pre-existing HUD `exhaustive-deps` warning), `npx vitest run` 443 passed, `npm run build` ✓, `npm run validate` 0/0.

pullRequests.title: T5.3: Custom JS theme-module URL loader (Option D)
pullRequests.body:
Closes #201. Parent feature: **F5 — Modularization & escape hatches**. Final task of the theme-customization Epic.

## What this adds

A new, **explicit, off-by-default, security-sensitive** opt-in — `config.theme.moduleUrl` (plus `moduleThemeName`) — that lets a host repo ship its own ESM JavaScript module exporting a Fluent `Theme` (or a `BrandVariants` ramp / seed hex). kbexplorer dynamically `import()`s it at runtime and registers the resulting theme(s) into the dynamic `THEME_MAP` so they are selectable and cyclable. This is the most powerful theming escape hatch — full programmatic control without touching the `.kbexplorer` submodule.

## Implementation

- **`src/theme/themeModule.ts`** — mirrors `src/engine/plugin-loader.ts` (the custom-provider stub): dynamic `import()`, structural shape validation, and a **single clear `console.warn` + no-op fallback on ANY failure** (network/404, wrong MIME, parse error, wrong shape) — the `THEME_MAP` is simply left unchanged. The importer is **injectable** so it's unit-testable against a local fixture module. Pure helpers (`isFluentTheme`, `isBrandVariants`, `themeFromBrand`, `resolveThemeModule`) handle the export-shape matrix; `generateBrandVariants` (T2.3) is reused for seed/ramp exports.
- **`useTheme.applyConfig`** now accepts `moduleThemes` and spreads them **last** — the module is the most specific escape hatch, so it overrides built-in/config/`themesFile` themes of the same name (precedence documented inline).
- **`App.tsx`** wires the import alongside the T5.1 external-theme flow: repo-relative paths resolve via `resolveImageUrl` like other host assets, absolute URLs used verbatim (`isAbsoluteUrl`). The import runs **independently** (no extra serial round-trip on the content fetch) and is a safe no-op on failure.
- **`CACHE_VERSION` 24 → 25** with a comment.
- **Docs**: documented the field and added a dedicated **CSP/security note** (script-src/connect-src, trust model, self-host recommendation, MIME requirement, "no `'unsafe-eval'`") to the configuration reference, plus pointers to the non-executable escape hatches (T5.1/T5.2) for lighter needs.

## Validation

- `npm run lint` → **0 errors** (pre-existing HUD `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` warning only).
- `npx vitest run` → **425 pass**, incl. 23 new `themeModule` tests: local fixture module resolves + registers a Theme; failure paths (import reject, wrong shape) log exactly one warning and are a no-op; full export-shape matrix.
- `npm run build` → `tsc -b && vite build` succeed.
- **Playwright (local mode, `VITE_KB_LOCAL=true`)**:
  - With a fixture module configured: the `neon` module theme appears in the cycle and **recolors** `--colorBrandBackground` (`#115ea3` → `#FF0480`), **zero** console errors.
  - With a missing module: app renders fine, `neon` absent from the cycle, **exactly one** `[themeModule]` warning (the only console noise is the browser's own 404 for the deliberately-missing file — the loader handles it gracefully).
  - Verification artifacts (temp config edit, public demo module, scripts) were reverted/removed; the regenerated manifest is gitignored.

## Notes
- No fixed-px sizing added (per AGENTS.md). 
- vitest stays `node`-only; pure functions + injected importer, no jsdom.

pullRequests.title: T5.1: load theme definitions from a dedicated host-repo file
pullRequests.body:
## Summary

Implements **T5.1 / F5 (issue #199)** — Option B: load a theme definition from a dedicated host-repo file.

Host repos can now point `config.theme.themesFile` at a separate theme file (e.g. `content/themes/extra.yaml` or `.kbe/theme.yaml`). It is fetched at runtime exactly like `config.yaml` and merged into the dynamic `THEME_MAP`, so a host repo can define or override named themes **without** editing the `.kbexplorer` submodule or inlining everything into `config.yaml`.

## What changed

- **New config field** `theme.themesFile?: string` (repo-root relative). Default unset ⇒ no fetch, pure no-op. Documented in `KBConfig.theme` and `DEFAULT_CONFIG`.
- **Pure, unit-testable helpers** in `src/theme/externalTheme.ts`:
  - `parseExternalTheme(raw)` — YAML → `ExternalThemeFile`, rejects malformed input gracefully (returns `null`).
  - `mergeExternalTheme(configTheme, external)` — pure merge, never mutates inputs.
  - `loadExternalTheme(themesFile, fetchRaw)` — fetch + parse, takes the fetcher as a param (testable against a mock).
  - `applyExternalThemeFile(configTheme, fetchRaw)` — convenience fetch+merge.
- **Wiring**: remote-loader fetches at runtime via `fetchFile`; local-loader merges from a new manifest field `themeFileRaw`; `generate-manifest` reads the referenced file; drift check tracks `themeFileRaw`.
- **CACHE_VERSION 22 → 23** (with comment) — cached content shape now includes external-file themes.
- **Demo**: `content/themes/extra-themes.yaml` + a `theme` block in `content/config.yaml`.

## Precedence (documented)

The external file is the more specific escape hatch, so it **wins** over inline `config.theme` for same-named theme keys (field-merged; tokens shallow-merged, external keys win) and for top-level `brand`/`tokens`/`default`. A missing / unreachable / malformed file is a silent no-op (warning only) and the `THEME_MAP` equals the config-only result.

## Validation

- `npm run lint` → 0 errors (only the pre-existing HUD `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` warning).
- `npx vitest run` → **393 pass**, including new tests for parse/merge/loader (override, missing-file no-op, malformed rejection) and `readThemeFile`.
- `npm run build` (`tsc -b && vite build`) → succeeds.
- **Playwright (local mode, `VITE_KB_LOCAL=true`)**:
  - File present: `forest` (defined **only** in the external file, absent from `config.theme.themes`) appears in the cycle and renders — `--colorNeutralBackground1: #0B1A0B`. No console errors.
  - File absent: `forest` is not selectable, falls back to default dark (`#292929`), `THEME_MAP` unchanged, no console errors.
- `node scripts/check-manifest-drift.js` → OK (idempotent + no drift).

## Notes

T5.3 (#201, custom JS theme-module loader) depends on this flow; the loader/merge helpers are kept clean and exported for reuse.

Closes #199

pullRequests.title: T5.2: Raw CSS override sheet from host repo (Option C)
pullRequests.body:
Closes #200. Parent feature: F5 — Modularization & escape hatches.

## What this adds
The "raw escape hatch" (Option C): a host-repo CSS file injected as the **last** `<link rel="stylesheet">` in `<head>`, so it can override `--colorNeutral*`, `--colorBrand*`, and `--kbe-*` CSS variables (and any other surface) the structured token system can't express — without touching the `.kbexplorer` submodule.

## Changes
- **`src/types/index.ts`** — new optional `branding.css?: string` (repo-relative path or URL), resolved via `resolveImageUrl()` like `logo`/`favicon`. Default unset; documented in `BrandingConfig` and the `DEFAULT_CONFIG` comment.
- **`src/hooks/useCssOverride.ts`** — `applyCssOverride` + `useCssOverride`, mirroring `useFavicon`:
  - Injects a single **managed** `<link rel="stylesheet" data-kbe-css-override>` appended to the end of `<head>` (wins the cascade).
  - Idempotent: updates `href` only when it changes (no needless re-fetch), never duplicates the element across re-renders.
  - **Removes** the element when config is unset; DOM-guarded (`typeof document`) so it's a safe no-op in the `node` vitest env.
- **`src/App.tsx`** — wired `useCssOverride` into the `Explorer` alongside `useFavicon`/`useThemeFonts`.
- **`src/api/github.ts`** — bumped `CACHE_VERSION` 22 → 23 (cached config shape now includes the css override path), with comment.
- **Tests** — `src/hooks/__tests__/useCssOverride.test.ts`: inject decision (set vs unset), href computation/update, remove + no-op when unset, no duplicate, no-DOM no-op.

## Validation
- `npm run lint` → **0 errors** (pre-existing HUD `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` warning only).
- `npx vitest run` → **373 passed** (incl. new pure-logic tests).
- `npm run build` → `tsc -b && vite build` **succeed**.
- **Playwright readback (local mode):**
  - **Configured** (`branding.css` → sheet setting `--colorNeutralBackground1: rgb(123,45,67)`): injected `<link data-kbe-css-override href="/...">` present, `injectedCount=1`, **last child of `<head>`**, computed `--colorNeutralBackground1` = `rgb(123, 45, 67)` (override won), zero console errors.
  - **Unset**: no injected element (`count=0`), token falls back to default, zero console errors / regressions.

## Notes
- No fixed-px sizing added (none needed).
- Heads-up: T5.1 may also bump `CACHE_VERSION` 22→23 / touch `types/index.ts`; my changes are scoped narrowly (new hook + wiring line + config field + CACHE_VERSION line) to minimize conflicts.

pullRequests.title: T4.2: per-page accent/theme via frontmatter (#198)
pullRequests.body:
## Summary

Final task of Feature F4 (scope layer). Adds **per-page (per-node) theming** declared in node frontmatter, restyling only the current reading page without mutating the global theme or document root.

Closes #198

## What changed

- **`KBNode.pageTheme`** (`src/types/index.ts`) — new optional, additive `PageTheme` shape: `accent` (brand seed), `tokens` (Fluent token deltas), and/or `theme` (named theme key). Absent → no change.
- **Parser** (`src/engine/parser.ts`) — parses optional `accent` / `tokens` / `theme` frontmatter into `node.pageTheme` defensively (untrusted YAML: non-string tokens and empty maps dropped; no fields → `pageTheme` left `undefined`).
- **Pure helper** (`src/theme/pageTheme.ts`) — `pageThemeTokenDeltas()` / `pageThemeStyle()` compute scoped CSS-var deltas relative to the active base theme. Layering (lowest → highest): named `theme` → `accent` brand recolor → explicit `tokens`. Reuses the T4.1 `clusterTokenStyle` scoped-CSS-var mechanism.
- **ReadingView** (`src/views/ReadingView.tsx`) — applies the page deltas as scoped CSS vars on the page container (keyed so navigating away remounts it and restores the global theme automatically). On the cluster-scoped header, page deltas are merged **after** cluster deltas so **page wins** for overlapping tokens.
- **App** (`src/App.tsx`) — threads the active resolved `fluentTheme` to `ReadingView` as the base for deltas.
- **CACHE_VERSION** 21 → 22 (`src/api/github.ts`) — node frontmatter shape now affects cached render.

No fixed pixel sizing introduced (per AGENTS.md). The global theme and document root are never mutated.

## Validation

- `npm run lint` — 0 errors (only the pre-existing HUD `exhaustive-deps` warning).
- `npx vitest run` — **367 passed** (new: 4 parser cases + 9 `pageTheme` helper cases).
- `npm run build` — `tsc -b && vite build` succeeds.
- **Playwright (real flow, local mode):** a node with `accent: "#C04040"` + `tokens.colorNeutralBackground2: "#3A1414"` rendered the page container with `--colorBrandBackground: #A73737` (accent-derived) and `--colorNeutralBackground2: #3A1414`, computed `background-color: rgb(58,20,20)` confirming the scoped var drives rendering. `document.documentElement` brand var unchanged throughout. Navigating to another node removed the `data-page-themed` container → global theme restored, no leakage.

pullRequests.title: T4.1: per-cluster token deltas as scoped CSS vars (#197)
pullRequests.body:
## Summary

First task of Feature F4 (scope layer — per-cluster & per-page theming). Adds an optional per-cluster Fluent token-delta map that shifts **only** that cluster's scoped surfaces (node cards, badges, reading header) via scoped CSS variables — the global dark/light/sepia/config themes are never mutated.

Closes #197

## Changes

- **`src/types/index.ts`** — extended the `config.clusters[<id>]` entry type and the graph `Cluster` interface with an optional `tokens?: Partial<Record<string, string>>` (Fluent token name → CSS value), reusing the same shape as `theme.tokens`. Additive/optional; `extractClusters` already spreads cluster fields so deltas flow through to `graph.clusters`. Updated `DEFAULT_CONFIG` comments.
- **`src/theme/clusterTokens.ts`** — new pure, unit-testable helper `clusterTokenStyle()` that turns a cluster's token deltas into a scoped CSS-variable style object (`--<token>` → value). Fluent v9 exposes each token as a CSS custom property of the same name, so setting `--token` on a wrapper shadows it for that subtree only. Missing/empty deltas yield `{}` (no-op).
- **`src/views/ReadingView.tsx`** — `findCluster` now also returns `tokens`; the reading `<header>` applies the scoped style.
- **`src/views/OverviewView.tsx`** — each cluster `<section>` applies the scoped style so its cards + badges shift.

Per AGENTS.md: no fixed-pixel sizing introduced (scoped vars only).

## Tests

New `src/theme/__tests__/clusterTokens.test.ts` covers: delta → scoped CSS-var map, already-prefixed names kept verbatim, undefined/empty → no-op (global theme untouched), undefined values skipped, input not mutated.

pullRequests.title: T2.2: build THEME_MAP dynamically from config brand/tokens/themes
pullRequests.body:
## Summary

Makes the theme map dynamic — built at runtime from `config.theme` — while preserving the three built-ins (dark/light/sepia) and existing switching behavior. This is the integration task of Feature F2, wiring the previously-dead `theme.brand` / `theme.tokens` / `theme.themes` schema (T2.1) into the live FluentProvider via the `generateBrandVariants` helper (T2.3).

Closes #193

## What changed

- **`src/hooks/useTheme.ts`**
  - New pure `buildThemeMap(config?: KBConfig['theme'])`:
    - Starts from the three built-ins (now `BUILTIN_THEME_MAP`).
    - **Global override:** if `theme.brand` is set, regenerates the dark/light base themes via `createDarkTheme`/`createLightTheme` (hex → `generateBrandVariants`; ramp object → filled to a complete `BrandVariants`), then spreads `theme.tokens` on top so explicit token overrides win.
    - **Named themes:** each `theme.themes.<name>` entry becomes a selectable theme keyed by its name, derived from its `base` (`dark`→`createDarkTheme`, `light`→`createLightTheme`, default `dark`), its `brand`, and its `tokens`.

  - With no brand/tokens/themes configured, the map equals `BUILTIN_THEME_MAP` (same object references) — behavior is byte-for-byte identical to before.
- **`src/App.tsx`** — passes the full `config.theme` to `applyConfig`.
- **`src/hooks/__tests__/useTheme.test.ts`** — adds pure-builder tests (no React rendering).

`CACHE_VERSION` is intentionally **not** bumped (deferred to T2.4 to avoid a conflict), and cycle/persistence semantics are unchanged beyond registering config themes.

## Validation

- `npm run lint` — 0 errors (pre-existing HUD `exhaustive-deps` warning only)
- `npx vitest run` — 331 passed (incl. 7 in `useTheme`)

pullRequests.title: feat(editor): source-of-truth editor with GitHub PR write-back handoff
pullRequests.body:
## Feature #152 — Source-of-truth editor → PR write-back

Implements **F5** (child of Epic **#147**, "Open, data-driven node-type engine"). Adds an in-app editor for a node's **underlying source-of-truth file** (the YAML/JSON entity file under `content-model/`) — **not** the JSON-LD projection, so F2's mappings stay pure and reversible.

### Architecture (the lightweight, secret-free, CLI-free handoff)
kbexplorer is a static, **secret-free** Azure Static Web App — it cannot and must not hold a GitHub token or write to git from the browser. So on save the editor doesn't commit; it hands the edited file off to GitHub's own **authenticated** web UI:

- **existing file** → GitHub web editor (`…/edit/<branch>/<path>`); the edited content is copied to the clipboard so the user pastes + commits to a new branch + PR.
- **new file** → GitHub create-file page (`…/new/<branch>?filename=&value=`) pre-filled with the path + content.
- a downloadable unified-diff **`.patch`** is offered as a portable fallback.

GitHub performs the authenticated commit + PR; the browser only builds links / produces text. **No tokens, no OAuth, nothing stored.**

### Changes
- **types** — add `NodeSourceFile` + optional `KBNode.sourceFile` (additive).
- **builder** — thread the originating file path + raw text onto entity nodes; unresolved stubs / derived / README / structural nodes carry none (so the affordance is simply absent for them — a safe no-op).
- **api/github** — bump `CACHE_VERSION` 16 → 17 (cached node shape changed).
- **engine/source-edit** (new, pure) — `canEditSource`, `resolveSourceFile`, `validateSourceContent`, repo-coord resolution, GitHub edit/new-file/handoff URL builders, and a **newline-agnostic** LCS unified diff (CRLF checkout vs LF textarea no longer looks like a whole-file rewrite).
- **views/SourceEditor** (new) — Fluent v9 dialog editor: validates the YAML/JSON parses before any handoff, shows the diff, and offers **Open PR on GitHub** / **Copy content** / **Download .patch**. Wired into the `ReadingView` header next to the source badge, shown only when `canEditSource(node)`.
- **tests** — `src/engine/__tests__/source-edit.test.ts` proving (a) the editor resolves a node's source file content, (b) the edit/new-file deep-link URLs are constructed correctly, (c) invalid YAML/JSON is caught before handoff, (d) nodes without a source file expose no affordance — plus CRLF/LF and unified-diff cases; and a `builder.test.ts` assertion that `sourceFile` is attached.

### Compliance
- **No pixels** in any added layout (vw/vh/rem/Fluent tokens only; `1px` borders excepted).
- Strictly **additive & safe** — read-only / repo-aware mode without a writable source behaves exactly as today.

### Verification
- `npx tsc -b` → **0 errors**
- `npm run lint` → **0 errors** (only the pre-existing `HUD.tsx` exhaustive-deps warning)
- `npx vitest run` → **327 passed** (28 files; +22 new)
- **Playwright live check** (`VITE_KB_LOCAL=true`): opened the **Ada Okonkwo** Person node, invoked **Edit source**, changed `role`, and confirmed the produced GitHub deep link (`…/edit/main/content-model/people/ada.yaml`) and the one-line unified diff reflect the edited source file. Screenshots captured.

Closes #152. Part of #147.

pullRequests.title: feat(content-model): cross-repo vocabulary/synonym mapping (#153)
pullRequests.body:
## Feature #153 — Cross-repo `@context` vocabulary/synonym mapping

Child of Epic **#147** (open, data-driven node-type engine). Unblocked now that F2 (PR #175) is merged.

Maps differing **per-repo vocabularies** to a canonical `@type` **across repos**, beyond a single repo's own `index/context.jsonld` — e.g. `cell` / `crew` → canonical `squad` — so the graph unifies concepts from repos that use different words, **while preserving each repo's native label**. The layer is **data-driven** and a **strictly-additive safe no-op**: with no vocabulary declared, graph output is byte-identical to before.

### How it works
- **Per-repo file** — an optional `index/vocabulary.jsonld`, a JSON-LD `@context` aliasing `term → canonical kind` (bare string or `{ "@id": … }`), authored exactly like the rest of the context.
- **Shared overlay** — a vocabulary supplied *independently of any single repo's files* (the cross-repo layer). `readContentModelSchema(src, overlay)`, `buildContentModel(src, overlay)` and `new ContentModelProvider(src, overlay)` accept it as raw `vocabulary.jsonld` text or a parsed `{ aliases }`. Overlay wins on collision.
- **Canonical resolution** — `canonicalKind()` runs in the builder's walk pass **before** convention/URN/cluster/entityType resolution, so an alias like `cell` (no convention/prefix of its own) resolves to `squad`, getting the squad URN base, cluster, and bespoke `SquadView`. Single-hop; self-mappings & JSON-LD keywords ignored.
- **Native label preserved** — `data` stays the verbatim record (so `data['@type']` keeps `cell`), and the builder surfaces the native term as `jsonld.nativeType` **only for aliased nodes** (non-alias output unchanged). Spine viewers show a small `native: …` badge via `nativeTypeOf(node)`.

### Changes
- `schema-reader.ts`: `SCHEMA_PATHS.vocabulary`, vocabulary parsing, overlay merge, exported `canonicalKind`.
- `builder.ts`: alias → canonical kind canonicalization + native preservation + overlay threading.
- `types.ts`: `Vocabulary`, `VocabularyOverlay`, `ContentModelSchema.vocabulary`.
- `content-model-provider.ts`: optional `vocabularyOverlay` arg.
- Spine viewers + `spine-data.ts` `nativeTypeOf` + `EntityHeader` badge + `.kb-structured-native` CSS (em units, no pixels).
- `CACHE_VERSION` 16 → 17.
- `content-model/README.md` cross-repo vocabulary docs.
- Demo content: `index/vocabulary.jsonld` + `cell`/`crew` entities unifying to `squad`.
- New `vocabulary.test.ts`.

### Verification
- `npx tsc -b` → 0 errors.
- `npm run lint` → 0 errors (only the pre-existing `HUD.tsx` exhaustive-deps warning).
- `npx vitest run` → **317 passed** (incl. 12 new vocabulary tests proving alias → canonical kind + correct viewer, native label preserved, cross-repo unification via both file and overlay, and safe no-op).
- **Playwright live check** (`VITE_KB_LOCAL=true`): two entities authored as `cell` and `crew` both render the canonical **SQUAD** type/viewer while showing `native: cell` / `native: crew`, and each lists the other under Related (unified via shared workstream). Screenshots captured.

Closes #153. Refs #147.

pullRequests.body:
Closes #188

## Summary
Wires `config.theme.default` into the initial theme mode resolution. Previously `useTheme` ignored `config.theme.default` entirely and always defaulted to `'dark'` when no `kbe-theme` value was stored.

Resolution order is now:
1. User's explicitly saved `kbe-theme` (localStorage) — always wins
2. `config.theme.default` — applied once config resolves
3. `'dark'` — final fallback

A config default is **applied but not persisted** (it isn't a user choice), so a later change to `config.theme.default` can still take effect for users who never picked a theme.

- `src/hooks/useTheme.ts`:
  - Added `readStoredRaw()` (returns `null` when nothing valid is stored) and a pure `resolveInitialMode(configDefault?)` helper.
  - `useTheme()` now returns a 4th element, `applyConfigDefault(configDefault?)`, which sets the mode to the config default only when no theme is stored.
- `src/App.tsx`: `Explorer` calls `applyConfigDefault(config.theme.default)` via `useEffect` once `useKnowledgeBase()` reaches `ready` (config is loaded async, after `useTheme` first initializes).

Did **not** touch the dark/light/sepia theme definitions or bump `CACHE_VERSION` (that's T1.3).

## Tests

- `config.default applies when no stored theme`

## CI concurrency hardening (F3 release-readiness infra)
`.github/workflows/github-pages.yml` previously used one global `pages` concurrency group with `cancel-in-progress: true`, so PR `test` runs cancelled every in-flight run (killing siblings' e2e mid-run). Now scoped per-ref:
```yaml
concurrency:
  group: pages-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}
```
PR runs only supersede older runs of the same PR; pushes to `main` (the only ref that deploys) get a distinct group and are never cancelled mid-deploy — preserving the Pages deploy contract.

> The content-model **source repo is being sunset** and is not in this repo. The schema + entity formats are therefore **defined by the fixtures** under `src/engine/content-model/__tests__/fixtures/content-model/`, designed to read the real files when they later land. The pipeline is a **safe no-op when no source is detected** — existing graph output is byte-identical (215-test baseline stays green).

## Sub-issues

- **Closes #160** — T2.1 Schema reader: parses `teamops.yaml`, `schema/{conventions,edges,lifecycle}.yaml`, `index/context.jsonld`. URN bases come from the JSON-LD context **only**; node kind comes from `@type`, **never** the file path; CURIE→URN + org/authority scoping.
- **Closes #161** — T2.2 `ContentModelProvider` discovery + node emission: walks entity files, detects flat vs nested org layout, builds a `(kind,org,id)` index, emits JSON-LD nodes via `buildJsonLd()`.
- **Closes #162** — T2.3 Edge resolution: scalar / array / composite / alias FK + derived (`shared-target`) + deprecated edges; unresolved refs stubbed with diagnostics; every edge typed with a `relation`.
- **Closes #163** — T2.4 Loader + build-time assembly: provider registered in `remote-loader.ts` + `local-loader.ts`; `readContentModel()` build path in `scripts/generate-manifest.js`; `CACHE_VERSION` 13→14.
- **Closes #164** — T2.5 Spine viewers Person + Squad (the original ask): bespoke viewers via the viewer registry; the example `PersonView` replaced with the real one + new `SquadView`.
- **Closes #165** — T2.6 Spine viewers Workstream, Mission, Priority, Cycle, Org.

## Design highlights

- **Relationships ride on `connections`.** The orchestrator ignores a provider's `edges` and `buildGraph` derives edges from each node's `connections`; the builder attaches typed connections to source nodes (and also returns a directed `edges` array for unit tests).
- **Reversible nodes.** `node.data` is the verbatim parsed record; the lifecycle band is surfaced on `jsonld` only; `buildJsonLd()` writes reserved keys (`@context`/`@id`/`@type`) last so `data` can't override them. `node.id === identity === <URN>`.
- **No-op guard.** Source is "present" iff `teamops.yaml` + `index/context.jsonld` exist; the provider checks this *before* registering any node types/viewers, so the registries (and layer output) are untouched when absent.
- **Repo rules.** Viewers are className-styled / SSR-safe with **no pixel sizing**; `CACHE_VERSION` bumped.

## Evidence

- **vitest:** 255 passed (215 baseline + 40 new) across 22 files — `schema-reader.test.ts` (10), `builder.test.ts` (17), `content-model-provider.test.ts` (3), `spine-viewers.test.ts` (7), `generate-manifest.test.js` (+3 `readContentModel`).
- **`npx vite build`:** green.
- New/changed files are **lint-clean** (`npm run lint` / `tsc -b` remain pre-existing red on `main` across untouched files — Bug #172, out of scope).
- **Playwright (local cached-data flow):** Person, Squad and Mission nodes render through their bespoke viewers with relationships resolved (verified against a staged `content-model/` dir + `generate-manifest` + `VITE_KB_LOCAL` build).

pullRequests.title: F3: Agile discovery & repo-structural nodes (#150)
pullRequests.body:
## Summary

Implements **Feature F3 — Agile discovery & repo-structural nodes** on top of the F1 open node-type foundation. All new behaviour is **additive and safe-by-default**: discovery is a no-op when the inputs (`.github`, `node-map.yaml`, structured files) are absent, so existing graph output and snapshot tests stay byte-identical.

Closes #150
Closes #166
Closes #167
Closes #168

## What landed

### T3.1 — Declarative `node-map.yaml` + heuristic inference (#166)
- `src/engine/node-map.ts`: a pure mapper. Declarative rules (glob/shape → `@type` → field/edge mapping) plus a **heuristic shape-inference fallback** that maps an *unmapped* structured file to a sensible JSON-LD node (`Workflow`, `SoftwareApplication`, `DependabotConfig`, `ParameterisedConfig`, `StructuredConfig`).
- Emits nodes via `buildJsonLd()`; identity URN reused as `@id`; **reversible** (full parsed object kept on `node.data`, `reconstructSource()` re-serializes).
- Root `node-map.yaml` example added (commented).

### T3.2 — `.github` structural discovery → repository node (#167)
- `src/engine/providers/structural-provider.ts`: discovers workflows, composite Actions, issue/PR templates, issue-template config, `CODEOWNERS`, `dependabot`, `FUNDING` (+ generic config via the node-map), and emits each as a node linked to the single repository (`repo-meta`) node via a **`structural`** relation edge (`type:'contains'`, `weight:5`).
- `registerStructuralTypes()` registers entityTypes (F1 node-type registry) **and** viewers (viewer registry). `dependencies:['work']` so `repo-meta` exists first. Safe no-op on empty input.

### T3.3 — Structural + generic-config viewers (#168)
- `WorkflowView` (triggers / jobs / steps) and `ActionView` (inputs / outputs / runs); generic configs fall back to the mandatory `GenericStructuredView`.
- `ReadingView` gains a **scoped** "Related structure" panel (only for `provider==='structural'` nodes) so the `.github` → repository edges are visible and navigable. No change to other node kinds or to graph data.

### Wiring
- `scripts/generate-manifest.js` collects `.github/**` + `CODEOWNERS` + `node-map.yaml` (size-capped).
- `local-loader.ts` / `remote-loader.ts` register `StructuralProvider` (guarded on non-empty input).
- `CACHE_VERSION` 13 → 14 (cached-data shape changed). *Note: a sibling session (F2 #149) may also bump this — expect a trivial conflict to resolve at merge.*
- No pixel layout sizing in the new CSS (`rem`/`em`/tokens; `1px` borders only).

## Evidence

**vitest — 252 pass** (was 215 on the F1 base; +37):
- `src/engine/__tests__/node-map.test.ts` — 21
- `src/engine/__tests__/providers/structural-provider.test.ts` — 14
- `src/engine/__tests__/structural-graph.test.ts` — 2 (asserts the **workflow → `repo-meta` edge** carries `relation:'structural'`, plus orphan-safe behaviour with no repository node)

**`npx vite build` — green** (default + local presets). `npm run build`/`tsc -b`/`npm run lint` remain RED across untouched files on `main` (Bug #172, out of scope); all new/changed files are type-clean and lint-clean.

**Playwright (`e2e/structural-nodes.spec.ts`, chromium) — 2 pass**, on the real local cached-data flow:
- The `.github/workflows/github-pages.yml` node renders `WorkflowView` (triggers `push`/`pull_request`/`workflow_dispatch`; 3 jobs with steps), the `Workflow · github-pages.yml` SourceBadge, and a **"Related structure → kbexplorer-template · configures the repository"** link — i.e. a workflow node visibly edged to the repository node. Following the link navigates to `#/node/repo-meta`.
- The `dependabot.yml` node falls back to the generic structured viewer and also links back to the repository node.

## Notes / assumptions
- The verified flow is **local mode** (`VITE_KB_LOCAL`), where `repo-meta` exists (WorkProvider with repo metadata). In remote mode `repo-meta` isn't created, so structural nodes orphan-connect to the graph hub via the existing safe fallback — acceptable and non-breaking.
- Two distinct map concepts kept separate: existing `nodemap.yaml`/`nodemap.ts` (repo files → file/content nodes) vs. new `node-map.yaml`/`node-map.ts` (structured files → typed JSON-LD nodes).

pullRequests.title: Fix baseline tsc/lint debt on main (#172)
pullRequests.body:
Closes #172

## What
Hygiene-only changes so the typecheck and lint gates are honestly green on `main`. **No runtime behavior changes.**

## Before / after

| Gate | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `npx tsc -b` | **52 errors** | **0** (exits 0 with the generated manifest present *and* absent) |
| `npm run lint` | **40 errors, 1 warning** | **0 errors** (1 pre-existing `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` warning retained — see below) |
| `npm test` (vitest) | green | green — 215 passed |
| `npx vite build` | green | green |

## Changes
- **Test typecheck:** added `tsconfig.test.json` (with `@types/node`) covering `src/**/__tests__/**` and excluded `__tests__` from `tsconfig.app.json`. Fixes `node:fs` / `node:path` / `__dirname` errors in the test files.
- **Generated manifest:** added an ambient declaration `src/generated/repo-manifest.d.ts` for the gitignored, prebuild-generated `repo-manifest.json`, so `tsc -b` is self-sufficient whether or not the manifest has been generated (TS2307).
- **`erasableSyntaxOnly`:** converted provider constructor *parameter properties* (`private x: T`) to explicit field declarations + assignments in `authored-provider`, `files-provider`, and `work-provider` (TS1294). The TS1294 errors were parameter properties, not enums.
- **Unused imports/locals:** removed across `HUD`, `HomePageWidgets`, `IconGallery`, `HomePage`, `createGraphNetwork`, `local-loader`, `nodemap`, `providers`, `remote-loader`, and two test files.
- **Griffel type errors:** the forbidden `borderColor` shorthand → accepted `border` shorthand (same rendered result); numeric `width`/`height` (`32`/`80`/`10`) → string values.
- **`remote-loader`:** `null` → `undefined` for optional `AuthoredProvider` args (TS2345); `let` → `const` (`prefer-const`); dropped 3 unused re-exported helpers.
- **`work-provider`:** dropped a gratuitous `as any` — `'repository'` is already a valid `DisplayMode`.
- **`NodeVisual`:** `Object.hasOwn(...)` instead of `Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty` (`no-prototype-builtins`).
- **eslint:** aligned `@typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars` with tsc's `noUnusedParameters` by ignoring `^_`-prefixed args/vars/caught errors (covers the `_config` / `_existingNodes` provider params).

## Suppressions (justified)
- **3 × `// eslint-disable-next-line react-refresh/only-export-components`** in `NodeVisual.tsx` for the co-located non-component exports (`FLUENT_ICONS`, `isFluentIconName`, `getVisNodeConfig`). This is an HMR-only DX rule with no runtime/correctness impact; the proper "fix" would mean carving a ~2,600-entry table and helpers out of a 5,000-line shared node-viewer module — a large, conflict-prone move while F2/F3 are actively editing that surface.
- **1 retained warning:** `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` in `HUD.tsx` is a pre-existing *warning* (does not fail lint) tied to the single-canvas HUD design; left untouched to avoid a behavior change.

## Concurrency
Kept every change minimal and mechanical to limit conflicts with the in-flight F2 (#149) and F3 (#150) branches. Branch is based on the current `origin/main` (F2/F3 not yet merged); will re-run both gates after any rebase before merge.

pullRequests.title: F1: Open node-type foundation — JSON-LD nodes + registries (#148)
pullRequests.body:
## Feature F1 — Open node-type foundation (JSON-LD nodes + registries)

Foundational feature of Epic #147: turns kbexplorer into an open, data-driven node-type engine. **F2 (#149), F3 (#150) and the cli repo's F8 (#18) are blocked-by this surface** — the contract is also published as a comment on #148 for early consumption.

All changes are **additive and backward-compatible**: a node/edge/provider that omits the new fields behaves exactly as before.

### What landed

| Task | Sub-issue | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| T1.1 | #154 | `KBNode.entityType` / `jsonld` (`@context`/`@id`/`@type` + LD props) / `data` bag; `buildJsonLd()` helper (`@id` reuses identity URN; `@type` never path-derived). |
| T1.2 | #155 | Open `DisplayMode` (`KnownDisplayMode \| (string & {})`, `'entity'` escape hatch); `NodeSource` gains a clean `{ type:'structured'; entityType; ref? }` variant; node-type registry. |
| T1.3 | #156 | Open `EdgeType`; `KBEdge.relation` / `Connection.relation`; 6-relation taxonomy (`leads\|staffs\|reports-to\|structural\|derived\|deprecated`) with `getEdgeStyle`/`getEdgeLegendKey`/`getEdgeWeight`; data-driven HUD legend. |
| T1.4 | #157 | Viewer registry (`src/views/viewers`): `registerViewer`/`resolveViewer` + mandatory `GenericStructuredView` fallback; `PersonView` example. |
| T1.5 | #155 | `getNodeLayer` is now registry-driven via `resolveNodeLayer` (built-ins pre-registered → byte-identical layer output). |
| T1.6 | #158/#159 | `ReadingView` `display:'entity'` resolves a viewer; `SourceBadge` handles `structured`; `CACHE_VERSION` 12 → 13; `content/node-types.md` contract doc; 33 new unit tests. |

### Design decisions
- **`NodeSource` opened via a clean `structured` variant** instead of `(string & {})`, to preserve exhaustive narrowing in `SourceBadge`/identity. New node types reuse `structured` + a registry `entityType` and never edit the core union.
- **Single styling source of truth** (`getEdgeStyle`) shared by the graph renderer and the legend, so they can't drift.
- **No runtime import cycle**: `types/index.ts` imports `resolveNodeLayer` (value) from the registry, which imports types **type-only**.
- **Off-by-default demo seam** `injectDemoEntities()` (`?demo=entities` / `localStorage['kbe-demo-entities']`) seeds person/team entities + relation edges for e2e evidence without polluting real graphs.

### Validation
- ✅ `npm test` — **209 unit tests passing** (33 new: JSON-LD/edge contract, node-type registry, viewer registry incl. SSR render, demo seam).
- ✅ `npx vite build` green (default + `VITE_KB_LOCAL` local build).
- ✅ Playwright (chromium): new `e2e/entity-nodes.spec.ts` (3) — PersonView resolution, generic fallback for the team entity, structured SourceBadge, **clean render with stale v12 cache present** — plus existing smoke/display-modes/navigation/layer-views (16) all green.
- Repo rules honored: no pixel layout sizing (viewer CSS uses rem/%/tokens; 1px borders only); `CACHE_VERSION` bumped for the new cached shape.

### Assumptions (resolved autonomously)
1. `content-model.md` is not present in this repo (likely a sibling-worktree artifact) → sub-issues #154–#159 treated as authoritative, adopting the 6-relation taxonomy + `kg://` `@id` + "@type never from path" rules from the brief.
2. `NodeSource` opened via the clean `structured` variant (narrowing safety).
3. Added the off-by-default demo seam to produce Playwright evidence.

Closes #148
Closes #154
Closes #155
Closes #156
Closes #157
Closes #158
Closes #159

pullRequests.title: fix(generate-manifest): detectHostRoot accepts template's actual package name and walks one level up
pullRequests.body:
## The bug

Vendored/submodule installs render the template's own bundled demo content instead of the host repo's content/.  detectHostRoot() never resolves correctly because of two compounding bugs:

1. Checks pkg.name === 'kbexplorer', but the template's own  package.json#name is kbexplorer-template — so the if-branch never executed for any real install.
2.  parentRoot = resolve(kbRoot, '..', '..') goes **two** levels up from  <host>/.kbexplorer, landing in the parent of the host repo.

## The fix

- Accept  'kbexplorer',  'kbexplorer-template', and  '@anokye-labs/kbexplorer-template' as template package names.
-  parentRoot = resolve(kbRoot, '..') — one level up, which is the host root.
- Honor a  VITE_KB_HOST_ROOT env override so consumers (kbexplorer-cli) can be explicit instead of relying on filename heuristics.

## Verification

- 176/176 existing tests still pass ( npm test).
- End-to-end: copied this script into a vendored install of the template inside the kbexplorer-cli repo. Before the fix, the manifest reported  Submodule mode: false and rendered 269 demo nodes from the template's own content/. After the fix, it reports:

    
  [generate-manifest] Submodule mode: true
  [generate-manifest] Repo: kbexplorer-cli  
  [generate-manifest] Content: 23 files
    

and the explorer renders the host's authored knowledge base correctly.

Bumps [actions/upload-artifact](https://github.com/actions/upload-artifact) from 4 to 7.
Release notes

Sourced from actions/upload-artifact's releases.

v7.0.0

v7 What's new

Direct Uploads

Adds support for uploading single files directly (unzipped). Callers can set the new archive parameter to false to skip zipping the file during upload. Right now, we only support single files. The action will fail if the glob passed resolves to multiple files. The name parameter is also ignored with this setting. Instead, the name of the artifact will be the name of the uploaded file.

ESM

To support new versions of the @actions/* packages, we've upgraded the package to ESM.

pullRequests.title: chore: repo setup + dependency bumps + KB agent upgrades onto main
pullRequests.body:
## Summary

Brings the repo-setup work onto current `main`. The original `feature/repo-setup` branch had diverged into a parallel re-implementation of the app; rather than replay that (which would regress main, the live/deployed branch), this rebases onto `main` and keeps only the genuinely additive pieces: repository governance files, the dependency bumps, and the kbexplorer KB agent/skill upgrades.

## Related Issue

Refs #

## Changes

- **Repo governance** (from #60, #70, #72): `.editorconfig`, `.env.example`, `.github/CODEOWNERS`, `.github/dependabot.yml`, `.prettierrc.json`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`, and PR-gating workflows (`dependency-review`, `linked-issue`, `pr-title`). `AGENTS.md` kept as main's app-dev guide.
- **Dependency bumps** (lockfile regenerated): marked 17->18, react/react-dom 19.2.4->19.2.5, react-router-dom 7.14.0->7.14.2, @eslint/js + eslint 9->10, eslint-plugin-react-hooks 7.0.1->7.1.1, globals 17.4->17.5, typescript 5.9->6.0, vite 8.0.1->8.0.5.
- **KB agents/skill**: kb-architect and kb-writer rewritten from the microsoft/skills deep-wiki plugin (MIT), new kb-researcher agent, new `.github/skills/kbexplorer/` skill, ignore `.env.kbexplorer`.

Excludes the Azure Static Web Apps deploy workflow (this repo deploys via GitHub Pages).

## Verification

- [x] Build/tests run
- [x] Manual or API verification completed
- Evidence: Verified against a clean `main` baseline. `npx vite build` passes, `vitest` 176/176, Playwright e2e (chromium) 46/46 including markdown-rendering visual tests (covers the marked major). eslint 10 runs the existing flat config and reports the same pre-existing issues as eslint 9 (no new errors). Pre-existing `tsc -b` / `eslint` issues on main are unchanged and not deploy gates.

## Checklist

- [ ] Linked issue referenced
- [x] Documentation updated if needed

Bumps [react-router](https://github.com/remix-run/react-router/tree/HEAD/packages/react-router) to 7.16.0 and updates ancestor dependency [react-router-dom](https://github.com/remix-run/react-router/tree/HEAD/packages/react-router-dom). These dependencies need to be updated together. Updates `react-router` from 7.14.2 to 7.16.0
Release notes

Sourced from react-router's releases.

v7.16.0

See the changelog for release notes: https://github.com/remix-run/react-router/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md#v7160

v7.15.1

See the changelog for release notes: https://github.com/remix-run/react-router/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md#v7151

v7.15.0

See the changelog for release notes: https://github.com/remix-run/react-router/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md#v7150

Changelog

Sourced from react-router's changelog.

v7.16.0

Minor Changes

  • Stabilize future.unstable_trailingSlashAwareDataRequests as future.v8_trailingSlashAwareDataRequests (#15098)

Patch Changes

  • Disable manifest path when lazy route dicovery is disabled (#15068)

  • Fix browser URL creation to use the configured history window instead of the global window. (#15066)

    • Pass the history/router window through to createBrowserURLImpl so custom window contexts keep the correct URL origin.

  • Fix useNavigation() return type to preserve discriminated union across navigation states (#15095)

  • Widen MetaDescriptor script:ld+json type from LdJsonObject to LdJsonObject | LdJsonObject[] to permit multiple JSON-LD schemas in a single <script type="application/ld+json"> tag emitted by <Meta /> (#15082)

v7.15.1

Patch Changes

  • Update router to operate on fetcher Maps in an immutable manner to avoid delayed React renders from potentially reading an updated but not yet committed Map. This could result in brief flickers in some fetcher-driven optimistic UI scenarios. (#15028)
  • Fix serverLoader() returning stale SSR data when a client navigation aborts pending hydration before the hydration clientLoader resolves (#15022)
  • Fix RouterProvider onError callback not being called for synchronous initial loader errors in SPA mode (#15039) (#14942)
  • Memoize useFetchers to return a stable identity and only change if fetchers changed (#15028)
  • Internal refactor to consolidate mutation request detection through shared utility (#15033)

Unstable Changes

⚠️ Unstable features are not recommended for production use

  • Add a new unstable_useRouterState() hook that consolidates access to active and pending router states (RFC: #12358) (#15017)

    • Data/Framework/RSC only — throws when used without a data router

    • This should allow you to consolidate usages of the following hooks which will likely be deprecated and removed in a future major version

      • useLocation
      • useSearchParams
      • useParams
      • useMatches
      • useNavigationType
      • useNavigation
      let { active, pending } = unstable_useRouterState();

      // Active is always populated with the current location
active.location; // replaces useLocation()
active.searchParams; // replaces useSearchParams()[0]
active.params; // replaces useParams()
active.matches; // replaces useMatches()
active.type; // replaces useNavigationType()

... (truncated)

Dependency Review Action 4.9.0

This feature release contains a couple of notable changes:

  • There is a new configuration option show_patched_versions which will add a column to the output, showing the fix version of each vulnerable dependency. Thanks @​felickz!
  • Runs which do not display OpenSSF scorecards no longer fetch scorecard information; previously it was fetched regardless of whether or not it was displayed, causing unneccessary slowness. Great catch @​jantiebot!
  • There are a couple of fixes to purl parsing which should improve match accuracy for allow-package-dependency lists, including case (in)sensitivity and url-encoded namespaces Thanks @​juxtin!

Full Changelog: https://github.com/actions/dependency-review-action/compare/v4.8.3...v4.9.0

4.8.3

Dependency Review Action v4.8.3

This is a bugfix release that updates a number of upstream dependencies and includes a fix for the earlier feature that detected oversized summaries and upload them as artifacts, which could occasionally crash the action.

We have also updated the release process to use a long-lived v4 branch for the action, instead of a force-pushed tag, which aligns better with git branching strategies; the change should be transparent to end users.

pullRequests.title: fix: position resize grip bars inside sidebar
pullRequests.body: ## Problem The sidebar resize grip bars were rendering on the grey border band instead of inside the dark sidebar content area. ## Root Cause The handle was positioned with \ ight: 2px\ from the parent's edge. The parent (expandedContent) has no border — the 6px border lives on the grandparent (hudContainer). So \ ight: 2\ placed the bars right at the visual border boundary. ## Fix - Widened handle hit zone to 32px (was 16px) for easier grabbing - Changed justifyContent to \ lex-start\/\ lex-end\ based on dock direction - Added 10px margin to push bars clearly into the dark sidebar area - Works correctly for both left and right dock positions ## Verification Closeup screenshots confirm bars are clearly inside the dark sidebar area, separated from the grey border, for both left and right dock positions. ---
